launches.title: Nucleo: Automated Cancer Diagnostics
launches.tagline: We help oncologists and radiologists extract insights from CT scans to characterize and treat tumors.
launches.body:
[Nucleo](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gR84avz0zkc)

**👉 [Learn more about Nucleo](https://nucleoresearch.com/)**

**👉 [Contact us](mailto:angelica@nucleoresearch.com)**

### **Problem**

Cancer is not only a biological disease; it is a **logistical failure**.

Cancer is responsible for 1 in 6 deaths \[1\]. ≃ 20% of those deaths happen simply because proven treatments start too late. The latest registry data show that the median **diagnostic interval** in the United States is about 36 days \[2,3\], while the median **time-to-treatment** initiation is roughly 32-41 days (≈38 days on average) \[4,5\]. So a typical American with cancer waits ≈ 9-11 weeks (65-80 days) before therapy actually starts.

A four-week delay after diagnosis adds 6–13% relative mortality; risk rises another ≈8 % for each additional 4 weeks (e.g. 12-week delay ≈ +26-30 % mortality) \[6\].

By automating key tasks in the oncological workflow we plan to cut 9-11 weeks to ≤ 10 days.

### **Solution**

The doctor imports the CT scan. Our AI-powered software automatically extracts key oncological metrics such as sarcopenia, body composition assessment, lesion volume, and target vs. non-target lesion classification.

Some results:

* Our segmentation is 2,500x faster than the manual one.
* We achieved State-of-the-art performance in sarcopenia detection.
* Our validation studies show a 98% agreement between Nucleo and medical experts.

launches.title: Anto Biosciences: A Foundation Model for Microbial Communities
launches.tagline: Making the microbiome computable.
launches.body:
We’re [Arvid](https://www.linkedin.com/in/arvid-gollwitzer/) and [David](https://www.linkedin.com/in/daviddegruijl/), and we’re building [Anto Biosciences](https://www.linkedin.com/company/anto-biosciences).

### tl;dr

Anto is building a multimodal foundation model for microbial communities, making the gut microbiome computable for the first time. We predict drug toxicity and efficacy across diverse populations and optimize molecules for universal efficacy — addressing the microbiome-driven causes of drug response and failures.

**Launch Video**: https://youtu.be/BDPp2wXiDbw

### The Key Problem

**We caught a cancer drug that worked in China but failed in U.S. trials. Same molecule, different microbiomes. $1B lost.**

This isn't an isolated story; more than a billion people are currently on medications where the microbiome dictates success or failure. The gut microbiome drives drug toxicity and efficacy, but pharma lacks the tools to understand and act on it \[10,11,13\]. Current methods to simulate the gut take months, cost millions, and rely on animal models that are too different from humans to be useful.

### About Anto

**We predict drug toxicity and efficacy across diverse populations and optimize molecules for broader efficacy—addressing the hidden, microbiome-driven causes of drug response and failures.**

Input any drug molecule. We tell you how people will respond. We show where it works and where it fails—by geography, age, or diet.

We predict:

* Population-specific efficacy (geographic, age-based, vegans vs. meat eaters, etc.)
* Failure mechanisms (specific microbial metabolic pathways) \[9,11\]
* Treatment response profiles across diverse populations \[10,14\]

And we don't just flag risk; we identify failure mechanisms down to microbial metabolic pathways and generate treatment response profiles across populations. Then we optimize the molecule for broader efficacy. Turning 20% efficacy into 80% becomes an optimization problem we can actually solve.

**Why we can do this:** We've pioneered quality-aware, goal-directed sparsification algorithms \[5,9,15\]. Microbiome data is 99% noise. We remove most of the noise and low-quality data through sparsification, leaving only the 1% that actually carries predictive power. That's how we make the microbiome computationally tractable. \[6,7,8,14\].

### About Us

[Arvid](https://www.linkedin.com/in/arvid-gollwitzer/) — Broad Institute of MIT and Harvard, ETH Zurich. Nature-published researcher who pioneered microbiome sparsification. Built the methods that make noisy microbial data tractable.

[David](https://www.linkedin.com/in/daviddegruijl/) — ex-ETH Zurich, J&J, BWH, Harvard Med, Gastroenterology. Struggled with current drug digestion models firsthand. Knows where current workflows break and how to fix them.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=95292&key=user_uploads/89898/3b2d64c2-dbc0-4bad-aad7-40b7995faeca)

We’re second-time founders who have lived this problem and published at leading AI conferences and Journals.

### Traction

We're working with pharma R&D to simulate drug–microbiome interactions and de-risk cross-border deals with population-specific efficacy predictions and response profiles. Our open-source tools and research \[1-9,14,15\] are widely adopted and taught in engineering and computational biology programs \[16\].

### What This Means for Digital / Computational Biology

**The microbiome is the missing layer in drug development.** Most orally administered drugs are modified by gut bacteria before reaching their targets. We're making this layer computable for the first time \[11-14\].

If you're building in digital biology, precision medicine, or drug development, let's talk. The microbiome affects everything.

### Our Asks

If you’re in drug development, cross-border deals, or translational medicine, we’d love to learn what microbiome requirements matter most to you. If you know teams in pharma and believe this product is cool, sharing / intros would mean a lot.

If you are in academia or microbiome research, try out our open-source tools \[5-15\]!

**Get in touch**: [founders@anto.bio](mailto:founders@anto.bio) | [anto.bio](https://www.anto.bio/)

### Our Research

Our foundational work spans high-performance genomic analysis \[1-4\], metagenomic classification algorithms \[5,9,14,15\], in-storage computing for microbiome data \[6-8\], and the first large-scale datasets for causal modeling of microbial ecosystems \[11,12\]. We've pioneered techniques that make microbial communities computationally tractable, including quality-aware sparsification that reduces noise by 99% while preserving predictive power \[5,9,15\]. Our recent work on therapeutic resistance \[10\] and AI-controlled metagenomics for clinical applications \[14\] directly informs our drug optimization capabilities.

**References:**

\[1\] N. M. Ghiasi et al., "GenStore: A high-performance in-storage processing system for genome sequence analysis," in _Proc. 27th ACM Int. Conf. Architectural Support for Programming Languages and Operating Systems_, 2022, pp. 635-654.

\[2\] N. M. Ghiasi et al., "GenStore: In-storage filtering of genomic data for high-performance and energy-efficient genome analysis," in _2022 IEEE Computer Society Annual Symposium on VLSI (ISVLSI)_, 2022, pp. 283-287.

\[3\] N. M. Ghiasi et al., "GenStore: A high-performance and energy-efficient in-storage computing system for genome sequence analysis," _arXiv preprint arXiv:2202.10400_, 2022.

\[4\] M.-D. Rumpf, M. Alser, A. E. Gollwitzer et al., "SequenceLab: A comprehensive benchmark of computational methods for comparing genomic sequences," _arXiv preprint arXiv:2310.16908_, 2023.

\[5\] A. E. Gollwitzer et al., "MetaTrinity: Enabling fast metagenomic classification via seed counting and edit distance approximation," _arXiv preprint arXiv:2311.02029_, 2023.

\[6\] N. M. Ghiasi et al., "MetaStore: High-performance metagenomic analysis via in-storage computing," _arXiv preprint arXiv:2311.12527_, 2023.

\[7\] N. M. Ghiasi et al., "MetaStore: High-performance metagenomic analysis via in-storage computing," _arXiv e-prints_, pp. arXiv-2311, 2023.

\[8\] N. M. Ghiasi et al., "MegIS: High-performance, energy-efficient, and low-cost metagenomic analysis with in-storage processing," in _2024 ACM/IEEE 51st Annual Int. Symp. Computer Architecture (ISCA)_, 2024, pp. 660-677.

\[9\] A. Gollwitzer et al., "MetaFast: Enabling fast metagenomic classification via seed counting and edit distance approximation," _arXiv preprint arXiv:2311.02029_, 2023.

\[10\] A. E. Gollwitzer, D. A. Subramanian, I. Tucker, and G. Traverso, "Steering the evolutionary game: Hierarchical control of therapeutic resistance in cancer treatment," in _NeurIPS 2025 AI for Science Workshop_, 2025.

\[11\] A. E. Gollwitzer, D. A. Subramanian, I. Tucker, and G. Traverso, "MetaOmics-10T: The foundational dataset to unlock causal modeling of microbial ecosystems," in _NeurIPS 2025 AI for Science Workshop_, 2025.

Available [here](https://bioethics.ethz.ch/news-and-events/news-bioethics/2024/12/decoding-the-human-microbiome-through-ai-controlled-metagenomics-promises-and-ethical-implications.html).

launches.body:
# **⏳TL/DR**

Rovi helps employees access high-quality, cost-effective healthcare. We text employees the best in-network options at exactly the right moment, and handle all the complexity.

* Our AI-enabled virtual care treats common conditions quickly over text or video.
* For complex care, our AI agents search across all in-network providers using millions of price and quality data points, then handle scheduling and logistics.
* Employees get rewarded for choosing high-value care through copay reimbursements and waived deductibles.

Launch video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mKNB0CF8_9Y

# **⚠️ The Problem**

Healthcare costs are crushing employers. 2025 is seeing a 9% rate hike, the worst in a decade. A 1,000-person company now faces over $1M in cost increases annually, compounding.

Employers’ only options are to cut benefits or redesign their entire plan. Both take months and frustrate employees.

What if Employers could offset these costs by adding benefits instead?

## **🤨 How is this possible?**

**Price and quality have no correlation in healthcare:**

* The same MRI: $700 at an imaging center vs $2,500 at a hospital. Same network. Same machine.
* The same knee surgery: $7,000 at a surgery center vs $25,000 at a hospital. Same surgeon. Often better outcomes at the surgery center.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=94971&key=user_uploads/1230817/7a7a2b27-4c82-410c-9744-82a5af6b1cc2)

**So why does everyone end up with the expensive option?**

1. **Hospitals own the referral pipeline.** They consolidated most primary care practices. When your doctor orders a procedure, their systems automatically directs it to their expensive facilities.
2. **Shopping is impossible.** Prices are hidden, provider directors outdated, quality is opaque. And when you're sick, calling twelve clinics is the last thing you want to do.

**Rovi does the hard work.** Our AI agents analyze terabytes of pricing data, research every provider's quality metrics, and surface options matching each person's preferences for cost, convenience, and availability. Making good healthcare decisions drives down costs for both the employee and the employer.

# **🎯 Impact**

We save employers 10-20% on healthcare spend while improving care outcomes and delivering a health benefit that employees love.

We've already signed contracts to roll out to thousands of employees across multiple employers for the 2025-2026 plan year.

## **🙏🏾 Our ask**

1. **Employers:** We have two final Q1 spots for self-funded employers. Introductions to employer benefits teams, brokers, health plans, and TPAs are welcome. Reach out to [santosh@rovihealth.com](mailto:santosh@rovihealth.com).
2. **Individuals:** [**Join our beta**](https://rovi.health/) to try our AI care concierge. Rovi will find you great in-network doctors whenever you need care. Virtual care coming soon.

## **👬🏾 Our team**

We're brothers on a mission to build AI-native health insurance that members love.

**Santosh** was previously building Cedar's affordability products, scaling to millions in ARR by closing enterprise deals with the country's largest hospital systems. Before that, he led a 30-person GTM & Customer Success team at AngelList. He’s also a licensed health insurance broker.

**Tarun** built foundational AI models to predict extreme weather events at UChicago, where he earned a Master's in AI and high-performance computing. He has a B.S. in biology from Cornell, and is obsessed with using AI to solve healthcare's messiest data problems.

Hello YC! We’re Suhail Parry, David Day, and Yash Raj from LunaBill.

_TL;DR:_ We built AI voice agents that automate insurance calls for healthcare billing teams. Fine-tuned on a dataset of over 1.2M call transcripts, our voice agents can handle insurance calls regarding claim-status inquiries, A/R recovery, and appeals follow-up.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=95408&key=user_uploads/2978935/704621ef-8701-4468-9167-c84f44c67f0a)

### **🚨 The Problem**

Every week, U.S. healthcare billing teams make tens of millions of calls to insurance companies to get claims paid.\
Each one averages **25 minutes**. That’s how hospitals unlock part of the **$260B in denied or delayed payments** every year.

But there’s a bottleneck:

* Reps can only handle a few calls per hour.
* Staffing is expensive and hard to scale.
* Delays cost millions in unrecovered revenue.

Meanwhile, every new hospital system or insurer integration compounds the complexity.

### **💡 The Solution**

LunaBill’s **AI voice callers** automate those phone conversations end-to-end.

Our voice agents:

* Handle **claim status checks, appeals follow-ups, and reprocessing calls** automatically.
* **Connect to any billing software** and dial claims that need to be worked.
* Run up to **100 concurrent agents** per client, like having a 100-person call center on demand.
* Deliver post-call summaries with the to-do steps, integrated directly into workflows.

They’re **fine-tuned on 1.2M+ real call transcripts**, understand payer logic, and sound completely natural.\
🎧 [Listen](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1jxi7GRUV4h1YDX8XkEYQdFzepboOQLq8/view?usp=sharing) to a real AI insurance call, see if you can guess who’s human.

### **⚡ Our Progress**

To date, LunaBill has automated **60,000+ insurance calls**, saving billing teams over **20,000 hours** and recovering **$30M+** in payments that would otherwise be lost.

Billers now can complete 300+ claim follow-ups per day — up from about 25/day before LunaBill, a \~12x productivity improvement.

LunaBill has partnered with **top healthcare systems** and **three of the biggest enterprise billing companies** across the country.

launches.tagline: Our healthcare system is failing the people it’s supposed to serve. At Eos AI, we are fixing that.
launches.body:
**TLDR:** We help hospitals turn their historical data into intelligence they can act on, catching operational and care breakdowns before they happen.

We create standardized data representations across all systems and time, retrieving similar trajectories to generate actionable forecasts so administrators and physicians can intervene early, save staff hours, and recover revenue.

**We are live (bless up!):**

In our early clinics, we are seeing \~3x productivity improvements in admin workflows and 37% revenue recovery by identifying early intervention points and automating operational workflows.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=98511&key=user_uploads/1928939/beca5e3e-27f7-475a-ae9b-f639169912f2)

#feedourdoctors

Today, hospitals have more data than any other industry in the world, but only 3% has been utilized to inform care decisions. And this is because healthcare is one of the most fragmented systems _somehow_ still in play:

* a single patient’s data sits across EHRs, imaging systems, payer portals, specialty-specific software
* it exists in completely different formats and distributions
* and none of the systems can talk to each other

**So what’s the solution:** move the intelligence to the data

Eos acts as an intelligent hub that helps healthcare systems collate all their data across fragmented sources, and make intelligent predictions on top of it. We first harmonize data across all platforms to create a unified and standardized patient data distributions and timelines, acting like a translation layer between different applications. Then we build a centralized index over it: a compressed representation that lets petabytes of data stay where they are yet allows us to search and reason across it as one system.

<https://youtu.be/i4jSgAeSfMA>

**What this enables us to do:**

Instead of treating the visit or document as an isolated instance, Eos looks at the patient’s full history and compares it to thousands of similar patients over time. It predicts how a case will resolve, triggers the required approvals and actions, and does so while reducing staff workload and recovering hospital revenue.

**The team:**

I’m Arya, I studied Math and CS at Caltech and did a lot of clinical AI and bio research at Stanford and Caltech. As long as I can remember, I have always wanted to be a doctor to help people (cliché, I know, but true nonetheless!), and realized the best way to help as many people as possible is to build a tool that every doctor can use. And super excited to have Professor Kuo from Stanford on board as well!

**How you can help:**

We are looking to scale our early successes. If you know anyone who works at health systems or independent clinics, would greatly appreciate an introduction!

Cheers,\
Eos AI :)

launches.title: Origin - Safer Cell & Gene Therapies with AI
launches.tagline: AI designed regulatory DNA sequences to program gene expression patterns
launches.body:
![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=97480&key=user_uploads/552024/dd558bc0-b110-466f-b603-d3acb473ba54)

Hey everyone!

We’re Yash and Malhar from Origin.

**TL;DR**

* Using AI to make cell & gene therapies **safer** by designing **DNA switches and dials**.
* Our model’s synthetic regulatory sequences program precise gene expression patterns in disease cells.
* We’re building the **largest** **proprietary dataset** consisting millions of experimentally validated regulatory DNA sequences across many different cell and tissue types.
* Our model **outperforms Google DeepMind’s AlphaGenome** at predicting regulatory element activity.

<https://youtu.be/jCN43gOy7x8?si=pkZU6sGREgiI-EHA>

**The Promise**

Cell and gene therapies have successfully been used to treat diseases like stage IV leukemia, retinal disease, and spinal muscular atrophy. However, their application is limited due to concerns around safety and efficacy. But this drug class holds the promise of being a **durable cure** for diseases like cancer, autoimmune, neurodegenerative, aging, and more.

**The Problem**

Toxicity events largely arise due to our inability to control **where**, **when,** and to **what** extent genes are turned on. Regulatory DNA sequences - enhancers and promoters - function to modulate the expression of genes. Current approaches to design these sequences involve naive methods like repeats of known motifs (patterns) and random ligation. These methods either **reliably yield poor candidates** or require **brute force to search** for even one promising hit.

<https://youtu.be/SDJFAJULTP0?si=IYXFHLAqU88CcaXK>

**Our Solution**

Axis – our state-of-the-art model – is trained to design and screen regulatory DNA to activate therapeutic genes in target disease cell-states.

Axis is able to rapidly sample **millions** of functional candidates when prompted by the cell-state. We’re currently testing these sequences in the lab to produce the **largest proprietary dataset** of synthetic regulatory elements, measuring their interaction with transcription factors and the phenotypic outcomes of gene expression.

**Axis’ sequences have the highest predicted expression in targeted cell types**

Using Malinois, an independent and in-vitro validated prediction model by the Broad Institute, we observed that Axis’ generated sequences had the highest transcriptional activity in the cell type they were prompted by.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=97480&key=user_uploads/552024/deb58343-aec7-4554-a176-d4ff1927da9f)

**Axis’ sequences contain known biological features**

Regulatory DNA sequences are activated when proteins called transcription factors bind to them at specific patterns of ATGCs known as motifs.

HNF4A is a known master regulator of hepatocyte and liver gene expression. We observed that in the generated sequences, its known motif most frequently occurred in HepG2 (liver cell line) targeted sequences.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=97480&key=user_uploads/552024/d4e9dc1a-47c7-4599-99f3-f0b4d8980c6a)

**Axis’ sequences have high diversity and explore a large design space**

Over 72% of our generated sequences have no BLAT alignment match up amongst themselves (using a 20bp threshold).

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=97480&key=user_uploads/552024/45c66f66-c144-46ac-aea9-2739e6aae6d9)

**Axis outperforms Google DeepMind’s AlphaGenome**

Axis demonstrates strong performance in predictive benchmarks measuring molecular properties of real regulatory sequences. These include measures like chromatin accessibility and transcription factor protein binding.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=97480&key=user_uploads/552024/f1b68778-ea47-44b1-a2fc-ee4ac39c25bf)

**The ask:**

If you know or are someone working on partnerships at pharmaceutical / biotech companies working in cell & gene therapies, reach out to explore:

* Partnering on regulatory sequence designs for target disease cells.
* Getting access to our proprietary dataset of sequence properties, sequence-protein interactions, and cell-state perturbations.

\
Feel free to reach out via email at [yash@origin.bio](mailto:yash@origin.bio)

name: Ruma Care
long_description:
Ruma Care automates all admin work for infusion clinics - starting with prior authorizations & copay assistance enrollment.

Biologics are expensive medications that cost $80-$150K+ per year per patient, and often need to be administered in specific settings called infusion clinics. Medical providers buy these drugs up front to secure pricing deals and safer inventory - they are reimbursed for the cost of the medications through the patients’ insurance. 

Current medical workflows aren't built for infusion clinics. Inventory, storage, transport, and billing is still managed through paper and excel spreadsheets. And because they’re so expensive, these specialty medications are denied by insurers at a rate of 37% each year. When they are denied, when workflows fail, or patients are infused before paperwork is cleared, providers don’t get reimbursed for the medication and are left covering the costs. Ruma Care solves this so clinics get paid, patients get treated faster, and care teams spend less time fighting forms. 

We do this in three ways: 
1. For each medication, diagnosis, and insurance combination, Ruma extracts the submission criteria required to get the drug approved by insurers. 
2. We pull out the correct forms, then automate the form-filling for prior authorizations. 
3. Lastly, we enroll patients in copay assistance programs, all in one workflow and platform. 

We turn a process that traditionally spans 70+ online portals, disparate paper forms, and manual phone calling into a single, streamlined platform. As we process prior authorizations, our models learn from denial patterns to understand exactly what insurers need to see to get a prior authorization approved.
one_liner: The operations stack for biologic infusion clinics

launches.body:
Ruma Care automates prior authorizations - we’re starting with clinics that administer the most expensive specialty medications.

Biologics are expensive medications that cost $80-$150K+ per year per patient, and often need to be administered in specific settings called infusion clinics. Medical providers buy these drugs up front to secure pricing deals and safer inventory - they are reimbursed for the cost of the medications through the patients’ insurance.

Because they’re so expensive, these specialty medications are **denied by insurers at a rate of 37% each year**. When they are denied, **providers don’t get reimbursed for the medication and are left covering the costs.** Ruma Care solves this so clinics get paid, patients get treated faster, and care teams spend less time fighting insurance.

### **Launch Video + Ruma Demo**

[**https://youtu.be/WwAa5VreO0M**](https://youtu.be/WwAa5VreO0M)

### **Problem**

Clinics can lose money when prior authorizations are denied.

Specialty medications like biologics cost $80K/year, which is why insurers are highly specific with requirements on access. Clinics are required to follow complex, hidden requirements such as:

* Trying cheaper drugs first
* Using specific drug brands or biosimilars
* Submitting through fax instead of portals

None of this is standardized. Each insurance company has different rules, and those rules change quarterly.

Clinics with high volume spend thousands of man-hours on completing these forms: the average prior auth takes 30 minutes and is still submitted through paper, fax, and phone.  When it is denied, the process can stretch into weeks or months of appeals, phone calls, and faxes.

During this time, clinics have already invested staff time and often administered high-cost drugs. If reimbursement is denied, that cost is never recovered.

### **Product**

We do solve the problems in 3 ways:

1. For each medication, diagnosis, and insurance combination, Ruma extracts the submission criteria required to get the drug approved by insurers.
2. We pull out the correct forms, then automate the form-filling for prior authorizations.
3. Lastly, we enroll patients in copay assistance programs, all in one workflow and platform.

We turn a process that traditionally spans 70+ online portals, disparate paper forms, and manual phone calling into a single, streamlined platform. As we process prior authorizations, our models learn from denial patterns to understand exactly what insurers need to see to get a prior authorization approved.

We are live across clinics in California and Nevada, and helped them cut the denial rates by 50% and reduce staff time per prior auth by 20x.

### **Our Story**

I quit my big tech job to work as a medical assistant. I wanted to understand why specialty medication access in America is so hard.

Christina experienced this as a patient herself, she spent years fighting payers to get on her biologic treatments.

We met at Yale’s CS50 class freshmen year and built a Yale dining app for food ratings. We took an entrepreneurship break to work in Big Tech (Apple, Uber, & Walmart), and startups (Medallion, Sigma), scaling Uber One across 13M+ users and building ML models for Siri and iPhone users. We built products for customers like United Health Care and the U.S. Health & Human Services. Now we’re building Ruma Care.

Here’s more about our story: [**https://substack.com/home/post/p-176970044**](https://substack.com/home/post/p-176970044)

### **New Launch of Formulary Navigator - Free tool for providers**

We spoke with 150+ providers. Every one said navigating insurance coverage rules is their #1 challenge.

So we created the **Ruma Formulary Navigator.**

Providers can enter the insurance plan, medication, and diagnosis, and instantly see coverage rules and prior authorization requirements. <https://ask.rumacare.com>

And we’re providing this for free to bring better access and knowledge to the medical community. 

If you know any hospital administrators, doctors, and coordinators at infusion clinics and hospital systems, we’d appreciate an introduction. 

Feel free to share this with any doctors, nurses, or medical admin staff struggling to understand new formulary changes in 2026: 

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=97245&key=user_uploads/2091502/a9b48325-b1a3-492a-9687-f6733602764b)

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=97245&key=user_uploads/1967697/468d68f7-8ea2-4b53-97b4-f2191f8510fe)

### **Our Ask**

If you know any hospital administrators, doctors, and coordinators at infusion clinics and hospital systems, and tech forward digital health clinics, we’d appreciate an introduction.

Thank you dearest gentle reader, [Meng Fei](https://www.linkedin.com/in/mengfei-shen/) & [Christina](https://www.linkedin.com/in/christina-lee-huang/)

Hey YC, we're [Rishab Jain](https://www.linkedin.com/in/rishab-jain-k/) and [Aditya Jain, MD](https://www.linkedin.com/in/adityajain2000/). 

Today, we’re announcing Prescience 🔮: health insurance for the age of abundant intelligence. Prescience is taking on United, Blue Cross, and every other incumbent to build the first health insurance company that doesn’t suck.

**TL;DR -** Prescience is a health insurance solution built for a world with AGI. We help cut premiums by 20%, offer $0 deductibles, include GLP-1s and other modern medicines, and have no hidden fees: we’re only paid when we save you money. We’re already helping some of America’s most ambitious companies save money, provide better benefits, and keep employees healthy so they can focus on their business. [www.getprescience.com](http://www.getprescience.com)

[youtube.com/watch?v=PBqyj9zP4BY&feature=youtu.be](http://youtube.com/watch?v=PBqyj9zP4BY&feature=youtu.be)

**The Problem**

Healthcare is a $6 trillion industry in America. For most companies it's the second-highest line item on their P&L, with costs rising about 15% every single year.

Employers keep paying more and getting less. Deductibles climb and the best benefits get cut. Even employees with "good" insurance still end up with denied claims, surprise bills, and debt.

Nothing changes because the entire industry is built to take a cut of your premium. When care gets more expensive, all of the middlemen make more money. They couldn’t care less if your people get more healthy.

**Our Solution**

Prescience is an AI-native health insurance that flips the incentive. Get a quote without speaking to middlemen, and get better health benefits at lower cost. That adds up to roughly **20% lower premiums**, and **better-than-platinum health benefits** like $0 deductibles, no middlemen, no fees. For YC companies, we have a Deal running with Free Wearables and GLP-1s covered.

Here's how we deliver. **Time Machine** is our reinforcement learning system trained on medical histories. The same way AlphaGo found "Move 37," a move no human would have played that turned out to be brilliant, Time Machine searches millions of possible health trajectories for each member and finds the non-obvious path that keeps them healthiest. Then it steers care toward that path: the right screening at the right moment, the right behavior, before a small issue ever becomes a hospital bill. We’re running a separate waitlist for YC companies who want to try Time Machine for personal use: <http://getprescience.com/time-machine-waitlist>

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=106632&key=user_uploads/3202469/9ec81a8e-0484-4a24-873c-9aafa87d8124)

Time Machine is paired with **Crystal**: our care navigation assistant in your pocket. As an MD, I’ve seen how patients struggle to manage the labyrinth of healthcare. Hours of phone calls and wait times. Pouring through confusion insurance documents. No more - Crystal can book visits for you, answer questions about your health, and pay your bills.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=106632&key=user_uploads/3202469/6d96fb46-38d8-4b14-934d-c070c77b13b4)

Instead of today’s health insurance experience that forces employers to talk to brokers for weeks just to get covered, employers on Prescience get a quote in days and a plan that automatically tracks savings and does filings. We don’t just sit around and collect money from premiums, but actually try to make your employees healthy.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=106632&key=user_uploads/3202469/869b2f99-6114-43c4-b8a3-4630545de430)

We are a real, full-stack solution. We’ve built out and partnered to deliver quotes, banking, HSA, MSO-PC, legal, compliance, network, risk, and any other solutions, We have a national team of top doctors who we negotiate with directly - no middlemen - and who we are able to offer fast payment, clear patient histories, and no admin paperwork. They in turn offer us heavy discounts we pass on to employers.

**The Team**

Rishab and Aditya are brothers and serial entrepreneurs. Rishab (CEO) studied CS & Neuro at Harvard, is an RSI alumni, won the International Science and Engineering Fair, and previously founded and exited an edtech company. Aditya (President/COO) earned his MD from Harvard Medical School, has been doing ML research since 2014, and is an Op-Med Fellow at Doximity.

Prescience aims to rebuild the entire $6T American healthcare industry into one that is proactive and prescient, not reactive. Our vision is to be both payer and provider, as our proprietary AI and data becomes ready to take on all of medicine.

Reach us anytime at [founders@getprescience.com](mailto:founders@getprescience.com).

launches.body:
**Problem:**

When a worker gets injured on the job, they see their primary doctor for treatment. The doctor treats them through a series of appointments until they reach maximum medical improvement - the point where no more treatment will improve their condition.

If the insurance company denies the claim, that's when the bottleneck kicks in. Both sides get attorneys, and they send all the medical records to a Qualified Medical Evaluator (QME) for an independent assessment.

The QME has to manually review these records. Some cases have thousands of pages, while others have tens of thousands. Even straightforward cases take 6-8 hours. Complex cases can take multiple days.

There are also agencies that take 40% of the revenue per case to do some of this administrative work for them.

Either way, doctors are missing out. They're either losing significant revenue to agencies, or they're spending so much time on paperwork that they can't handle more cases.

**Solution:**

Docura Health automates the entire workflow:

Upload medical record PDFs and case documents → we generate fully compliant record reviews and reports in 30 minutes

Automate patient history collection calls that admin staff normally handle before evaluations

Doctors handle significantly more cases while keeping far more revenue per case.

\*\*Demo Video:\*\*\
<https://youtu.be/y2CU0QIXSS4>

**Progress:**

We’re live with multiple healthcare practices and med-legal expert groups. Providers working with us have doubled their case volume from the last month and some even process over 50k pages per month.

* If anyone knows any qualified medical evaluators or independent medical evaluators that are orthopedic surgeons, pain medicine doctors, or internal medicine doctors, would appreciate warm intros.

launches.body:
We're Yue and Oded, the founders of Strand AI ([strandai.com](http://strandai.com)).

## TL;DR

Strand AI develops foundation models that generate missing bio-data about patients. With this imputed data, pharmaceutical companies can select better patients for their drug trials and shave months from their drug launch timelines. We’ve already trained a multimodal foundation model that integrates spatial biology modalities, beating SOTA, at a fraction of the cost.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=98178&key=user_uploads/1489450/997163fb-e9dc-478b-a083-a1d128fd25af)

## The Problem

Every year, $60-100B is invested into clinical trials that do not result in approved therapies. 9 out of 10 drug trials fail. These drugs work by targeting specific biological pathways, but not every patient has the same pathways active. When a trial can't tell who has what, responders get diluted by non-responders, the effect washes out, and the trial fails. The key to selecting the right patients is multimodal data: genomics, RNA, proteins, imaging, clinical outcomes. But for any given patient, most of this data is missing. You might have their RNA expression but no pathology slides. Their genomics but not their clinical outcomes. The full picture is never there.

Yue saw this firsthand. Before starting Strand AI, he was building foundation models on the largest patient dataset in existence, working directly with the founders of Tempus AI. Whether predicting patient drug response, modeling disease progression, or finding new mechanisms of action, every task hit the same wall. Even with the largest dataset in existence, there simply wasn't enough to make good predictions.

The easy answer is "collect more data." But multimodal patient data is expensive, invasive, and often impossible to get. Patients drop out of trials, skip evaluations, or are part of rare populations where the data simply doesn't exist.

## Our Insight

The good news is that there's enough paired data across modalities that the missing biology can be intelligently and accurately predicted from what's already there. Strand AI builds cross-modal prediction models that take what you already have and predict what you don't.

We can efficiently evaluate which modalities we're able to predict accurately for a given dataset, so teams know exactly where we can fill gaps and when new measurements are needed. This lets pharma and biotech teams take their incomplete clinical cohorts and unlock precision that would otherwise be locked behind missing data.

<https://youtu.be/VUkR15k8X1E>

## What We've Built

We recently trained from the ground up a foundation model that predicts spatial proteomics from routine H&E staining. It beats state-of-the-art and we did it in under 6 weeks, at a fraction of the cost of comparable efforts. We were able to achieve this due to our deep, hands-on experience with both the data and the infrastructure. We’ll be deploying this model at scale for pharmaceutical and biotech companies to enrich their patient data.

## About Us

Before Strand AI, we worked shoulder-to-shoulder at Enable Medicine, where we built the platform for petabyte-scale multimodal spatial biology data — single-cell resolution imaging, spatial transcriptomics, spatial proteomics, and clinical metadata — all linked at the patient level. We indexed, analyzed, and served the largest spatial biology datasets in existence. That work gave us an unusually deep understanding of what multimodal biological data actually looks like at scale — what's missing, what's noisy, and what it takes to make it useful.

Oded has been programming since he was 8. At Enable Medicine, he led product to build the spatial biology platform end-to-end.

launches.title: CellType: The Agentic Drug Company
launches.tagline: What takes big pharma years, we aim to do in weeks.
launches.body:
We're David and Ivan — we built this technology at Yale and are now turning it into a company.

AI is fundamentally changing how software gets built. Drug discovery is next.

# TL;DR

We're building an agentic drug company: **foundation models that learn human biology + AI agents that run the full discovery pipeline**. Instead of mice and cell lines, we simulate what will happen in patients — before you run the trial.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=97885&key=user_uploads/1493577/d81c7718-831b-4ed3-8b76-c1f050d31193)

Our core technology, Cell2Sentence ([ICML 2024 paper](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v235/levine24a.html) · [C2S-Scale paper](https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/2025.04.14.648850v4)), was [featured by Google](https://blog.google/technology/ai/google-gemma-ai-cancer-therapy-discovery/) and shared by **Google CEO Sundar Pichai** (7M+ views). It teaches LLMs to understand cellular biology, and we've already used it to **discover and validate a new cancer treatment signal**.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=97885&key=user_uploads/1493577/0b848ed1-640a-4601-bd61-54ab7d22f4f1)

# The Problem

90% of drugs fail in clinical trials. Most of that failure traces back to one thing: our preclinical models don't match humans. Mice and cell lines don't represent what actually happens in patients, so teams spend years and billions optimizing against the wrong reality.

And the process itself is broken: massive teams, manual workflows, siloed data, and painfully slow iteration. A typical drug takes 10+ years and $2B+ to develop. Most fail anyway.

[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MBlSLzVBnH8](https://img.youtube.com/vi/MBlSLzVBnH8/0.jpg\)%5C%5D\(https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MBlSLzVBnH8\))

# Our Approach: AI Agents + A Virtual Human

We're building a new type of drug company from scratch around AI.

**The vision: AI agents do the work, humans steer the science.** Today, drug R&D means hundreds of scientists manually digging through literature, analyzing data, generating hypotheses, designing experiments, and coordinating with contract labs. We're replacing that with autonomous agents that execute end-to-end.

**The technology:** we taught LLMs to understand biology. Our core insight is that biology has structure, like language — gene expression profiles are sentences, cellular states encode meaning, drug responses are transformations. We built Cell2Sentence to convert single-cell biology into a form that foundation models can learn from. Unlike protein-centric approaches (AlphaFold, Boltz, ESM), we model the whole biological system — cells, tissues, microenvironments, and drug-cell interactions. **Proteins are parts; we model the machine.**

**The product:** a virtual human — a computational model of human biology you can test drugs on before touching a real patient. At every stage of development, you can ask "what will happen in humans?" and get an answer grounded in real human data, not proxies. Target discovery, toxicity prediction, translational prediction, patient stratification, virtual trials.

Our work is published at ICML 2024.

# Validation: We Discovered a New Cancer Treatment Signal

We didn't just build a model, we used it to find something real.

We screened 4,000+ drugs and predicted a novel hit: a drug that could help turn "cold" tumors "hot" (more visible to the immune system) — something that wasn't previously known. We then validated it in the lab — both in cell lines and in intact human tumor microenvironments that mirror what happens in patients. **The prediction held up.**

This is the kind of result that takes traditional R&D teams years.

# Traction

We're **already working with Top 10 pharma** — and every deal has been **100% inbound**. They saw the work and reached out to us.

# Our Team

We're two founders with deep expertise in biology + AI who invented the underlying technology together at Yale.

**David van Dijk, PhD:** Yale Professor, 11,000+ citations, published in Cell, Nature, ICML, and NeurIPS, turned down Google to build CellType.\
**Ivan Vrkic:** co-built the core tech at Yale (published at ICML), built software to control CERN's Large Hadron Collider, and led large-scale foundation model training at a biotech company.

# Our Ask

If you're a pharma or biotech team that wants to de-risk discovery and development — especially around translational and clinical prediction — we'd love to talk. We're also looking for data partners and exceptional bio and ML builders who want to help build an agentic drug company from scratch.

[david@celltype.com](mailto:david@celltype.com)

launches.body:
Hey YC! We’re Ab, Sam and Zac.

**We are building the logistics infrastructure to modernize healthcare operations, beginning with physician scheduling and care coordination, to combat rampant inefficiencies in healthcare.**

[**https://youtu.be/SXIaP6D1PJo?si=ERtC2Uq2_l92gqbS**](https://youtu.be/SXIaP6D1PJo?si=ERtC2Uq2_l92gqbS)

**Our Beginning:**

This all began when a doctor at Johns Hopkins told us that residents and attending physicians spend **hundreds of hours** each year scheduling. Thus began our **physician** **scheduling service**. 

We built an internal **Optimization Programming Language** that lets us create complex schedules far faster than traditional methods. Our clients now review schedules we build, rather than spend hundreds of hours manually creating them.

Through our scheduling, we have built trust in healthcare logistics across major academic health systems with active contracts at **Mass General**, **Johns Hopkins**, **UT Southwestern**, **LA General**, **UCF** and more! We are actively growing and onboarding new partners.

**Revelations I:**

These relationships revealed that healthcare administration, more generally, is unbelievably manual, disjointed, and inefficient. That’s why we have expanded our scope to tackle clinical care coordination. We have separated clinic operations into two segments: **The Patients**, and **The Resources**. 

**The Patients:**

The patient journey at most clinics begins with a referral process that leads to a triaging bottleneck before a patient can be seen. Only once this is complete can the complex systems for evaluation and treatment tracking begin.

**The Resources:**

Managing and tracking personnel, rooms, and time is difficult for even the best administrative teams.

**The Secret**

The problem with healthcare is not on the demand side, it is on the supply side. **Care coordination is the bridge between patient needs and hospital resources.**

**Revelations II:**

With our design partners at **UCSF and other major healthcare systems**, we are building patient triaging and provider management systems to improve and automate care coordination, while reducing administrative burden.

We aim to modernize healthcare operations. As our partnerships grow and our scope expands, we will become the key player in **bringing healthcare operations into the future.**

**The Team**

We are a team of award-winning mathematicians, computer scientists, and logistics experts from Johns Hopkins University.

Our CEO, **Sam Oberly**, is an expert in predictive logistics with a civilian service medal for his logistical coordination algorithm development. He is a published mathematician, trained at Hopkins and Cambridge. (<https://www.linkedin.com/in/sam-oberly/>)

Roughly 10 million of those are joint replacement surgeries that receive planning over 2 - 5 business days. This limits the use of robots and 3D printed guide systems and adds time and interruptions between when a surgeon sees the patient and when the plan can be discussed with the patient. \
\
15 million surgeries are acute fractures. Time-sensitive surgeries of high complexity, that have the same source medical imaging data, but lack the planning workflows to plan outcomes and take the cognitive load off of the surgeons. \
\
They have to figure out how to treat their patient during the surgery, which leads to a lot of trial and error, wasted operating room time, wrong implants, complications and revision surgeries. The number 1 request from surgeons we have received was for them to be able to have patient-specific plans for these complex cases.\
\
When surgeries become plannable instantly, it opens the door to planning multiple scenarios and giving surgeons peace of mind that they know how to face the surgery they are entering in the operating room.

\*\*When planning can be done instantaneously, all surgeries can be planned in time.\*\*\
\

launches.body:
One of the hardest things to scale in healthcare is also one of the most basic: making sure patients and clinicians actually understand each other.

**TL;DR**: [Opalite](https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/opalite-health) helps healthcare providers communicate with patients who don't speak English with an AI medical interpreter that saves 20% time per session and millions annually on interpretation costs.

Launch Video: <https://youtu.be/_AMvW9Co9do?si=YTKM4wGUgz0-qmrs>


**🤯 The Problem**

When patients and providers don't speak the same language, critical medical information gets lost - symptoms are misunderstood, diagnoses are wrong, and patients can't follow treatment plans. 

Over 30 million people in the US have limited English proficiency, and these communication breakdowns lead to worse outcomes across nearly every measure. Federal law requires healthcare providers to offer interpretation to solve this, but the current solution - a human medical interpreter - doesn't work. 

Getting an interpreter takes up to 30 minutes, if one is available at all. When they do connect, interpreters frequently omit or mistranslate important details, especially in fast-moving or complex visits. It also costs hospitals upwards of $1-2M per year. The system is expensive, slow, and unreliable, creating gaps in communication that put patients at risk and increase liability for healthcare organizations.


**❤️ The Solution** 

Opalite is an AI-powered medical interpreter that helps healthcare professionals communicate with non-English-speaking patients. It’s available instantly, 24/7, so care doesn't have to wait for an interpreter to connect.

Opalite works directly inside clinical workflows, including the EHR, allowing providers to communicate in real time without switching tools or interrupting visits. Translation quality is proven to be superior to certified medical interpreters, but at more than 50% lower cost than traditional services. Opalite also generates visit documentation automatically, reducing the amount of charting providers need to do after each encounter.


**📊 Our progress:** 

Opalite is currently used daily by patients and providers across 10+ states. Our customers include hospitals, community health centers, home health organizations, telehealth providers, and clinics. We are also set to roll out in a large healthcare enterprise within the next two months. 


**💡 Our Story**

[@Cathleen Kuo](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/1543800) is a physician and the child of immigrants who don't speak English. She has seen the language barrier issues from both sides - watching her parents struggle to communicate with their doctors, and later experiencing firsthand how language barriers compromise the care she can deliver as a physician.

[@Alex Mehregan](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/657915) is a former software engineer at Apple where he worked on Apple Intelligence and the updated Siri - software that touches many millions of users every day. He is a 2x founder and Berkeley EECS alumni.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=97038&key=user_uploads/1543800/8c237420-8e5d-47b5-8721-05769cabb1d9)


**🙏 Our Ask:**

* Know healthcare administrators, clinic directors, or hospital C-suites? We’d appreciate an intro.
* Building a product that serves patients or providers? If language barriers affect your users, let’s chat. 
* Have experience with medical interpreters (as a provider or patient)? Your feedback would be invaluable.

**Reach out at**: [cathleen@opalitehealth.com](mailto:cathleen@opalitehealth.com) & [alex@opalitehealth.com](mailto:alex@opalitehealth.com)

**Visit us**: <https://opalitehealth.com>

Hey YC! We’re **Meer**, **Vishvam**, and **Sanjit** — the founders of **Prana**. ([pranadoc.com](http://pranadoc.com))

TL;DR:\
Prana is the "Always-On" AI Doctor. We replace the reactive annual physical with continuous, proactive monitoring. We connect to your medical records and wearables to detect "clinical drift" (like rising blood pressure or glucose) weeks before it becomes an emergency.

**The Problem**\
Primary care today is episodic and reactive: you only see a doctor when you are already sick. Real health issues don’t happen overnight; they happen in the "drift" between visits. Because data is siloed (your Oura ring doesn’t talk to your Epic chart), doctors miss the full context of your health, often leading to late detection of metabolic disease and chronic illness.

**The Solution**\
Prana acts as a 24/7 intelligent layer on top of your health data.

* **Unified Profile:** We aggregate your history (EHRs via Fasten) and real-time biometrics (Wearables via Junction) into a single clinical timeline.
* **Continuous Monitoring:** Instead of waiting for you to complain, our AI acts as a background monitor, analyzing your data for anomalies and drift.
* **Doctor-in-the-Loop:** When risks are detected, the system escalates to our physician network for immediate intervention—turning passive data into active care.

<https://youtu.be/T0NoisWj0Ic>

**The Team** We are combining clinical expertise with high-frequency data engineering.

**TL;DR:** Patientdesk handles inbound and outbound calls, scheduling, live insurance verification, claims submission, and billing for dental clinics — all in one system. We grew from $17K to $50K MRR in 8 weeks and have driven $1.8M in incremental revenue for our customers.\

<https://youtu.be/1liipoEyTuk> 

👋 **Hi, we're Oncel, Şan, and Emre.**

We've been best friends since 2016. All three of us ranked #1 nationwide out of 1.2 million students on the Turkish national exam, ended up in the same high school dorm room, and have been working together ever since. Before Patientdesk, we ran a dental marketing agency and our own call center for two years. We didn't find this problem. It found us.

🔴 **The problem**

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=98988&key=user_uploads/2594817/da263c64-fc8a-45ab-a59f-a1bbb5702156)

The US dental industry processes $189 billion in services annually across 135,000 clinic locations. Yet the average practice runs on five disconnected tools that don't talk to each other. The consequences are severe:

* 15% of insurance claims are denied, 80% of those denials are preventable
* 65% of denied claims are never resubmitted
* Front desk staff spend up to 20 hours per week on manual insurance verification alone

Every time data moves between tools, a human moves it manually. A wrong code, a missing attachment, a verification that never made it to the claim. The clinic doesn't get paid. This is not a staffing problem. It's a coordination problem. And you can't fix a coordination problem by adding more tools.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=98988&key=user_uploads/2594817/e7b525fc-ccb3-434f-be85-43a83ae665fd)

✅ **What we built**

Patientdesk is the AI-native operating system for dental practices. We started with the front office and we're building toward owning the entire stack.

Today we handle:

* **Inbound and outbound calls** — 24/7 coverage, no missed calls, no voicemails
* **Scheduling** — books directly into the practice management software
* **Live insurance verification** — we are the first system to verify insurance during the booking call, in real time, without any manual handoff
* **Claims submission and denial follow-up** — we submit claims directly and follow up on denials automatically so clinics stop leaving money on the table
* **Payments and billing** — automated reminders and collection

Our goal is to replace the $15,000/month stack clinics currently use with a single platform starting at $7,500/month.

📈 **Traction**

* $17K → $50K MRR in 8 weeks, 39% MoM growth
* $1.8M in incremental revenue driven for customers since September 2025
* 60+ clinics live across the US, Australia, and the UK

launches.tagline: All-in-one patient intake system built for real dental workflows.
launches.body:
We’re **Oncel, San, and Emre**, founders of **Patientdesk**.\
\
One quick data point before we get into it.

In December alone, one of our customers generated $350k in revenue directly from Patientdesk bookings.\
\
**TL;DR**

Patientdesk is a **patient-aware AI booking system for dentists.** We handle calls, bookings, payments, and **real-time insurance verification during the call** so clinics capture more revenue and fill their calendars with higher-value appointments.\
\
We are growing rapidly, especially in the **US**. We are live in **60+ clinics** across the US, Australia, and the UK, partnered with **3 major practice management systems**, and have been **invited to exhibit at the world’s largest dental fairs like ADX**.

## <https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eTQU6bzZ-Ww>

## **The Problem**

Dental practices leak revenue at the front desk.

Calls come in while teams are busy or after hours. Try calling a dentist in the evening or on the weekend and it will usually go straight to voicemail.

Patients do not wait. They move on.

This becomes even more painful with paid acquisition. Clinics invest heavily in ads, but often follow up hours or days later. By then, the patient is gone.

What’s left:

* Missed opportunities
* Underutilized provider calendars
* High CAC with poor conversion

This bottleneck has existed for decades and worsens as clinics scale.

## **What We Built**

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=97818&key=user_uploads/2594817/80f45110-8b4d-47e2-8824-15d30704d9b2)

Patientdesk is an AI booking system built specifically for dental clinics.

Instead of solving one piece of the workflow, we run **patient intake end to end**, without increasing staff workload or forcing clinics to change how they operate.\
\
**Unlike generic booking tools, Patientdesk is patient-aware.**

It understands who is calling, their history with the clinic, and what type of appointment they are asking about, so conversations are handled with the right context instead of starting from zero every time.

Patientdesk covers:

* Incoming patient calls
* Intake and qualification
* Appointment booking
* **Insurance verification in real time during the call**
* Payments and deposits

All within a single system.

We are the first system that verifies insurance live during the call within a couple of seconds. This lets clinics confirm coverage and pricing immediately, instead of booking blindly or calling patients back later, which is where many high-value cases drop off.\
\
Patients get answers immediately instead of waiting for callbacks or manual checks.

## **How It Works**

Patientdesk integrates directly with major clinic management systems across the US, Australia, and the UK.

We have **active partnerships with three major practice management systems**, allowing us to book, update, and verify information directly inside clinic systems.

When something needs to be booked, checked, or updated, it happens automatically inside the clinic’s existing system.

If a patient asks about coverage, **insurance is verified on the spot**, typically within seconds.\
No follow-up calls. No dropped patients.

After the visit, Patientdesk continues to work:

* We follow up with patients
* When a payment is due, we handle it automatically

The front desk is no longer a bottleneck and becomes a revenue engine.

## **Traction**

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=97818&key=user_uploads/2594817/c67cb867-68bb-4fbd-9106-43aebb53e2d7)

* Live in **60+ clinics**, primarily dental, across the US, Australia, and the UK
* Growing rapidly in the **US dental market**
* Handling real patient calls every day
* Partnered with **3 major practice management systems**
* Invited to **the largest dental conferences and trade shows globally**

Patientdesk is already the core infrastructure for the clinics we support.

## **🔍 Why We’re Building This**

We did not arrive here by theory.

Before Patientdesk, we spent years working directly with clinics. We built workflows, trained front desk teams, and operated our own call center.

We saw that while there are tools for individual steps like phones, bookings, and insurance, nothing handles patient intake completely in one system.

Patientdesk came from that gap.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=97818&key=user_uploads/2594817/2b5239db-0031-4bf5-98d0-397bb72c06ad)

## **🤝 Our Ask**

If any of the below resonate, we would love your help:

* Introductions to dental groups, DSOs, or healthcare operators
* Feedback on positioning such as AI receptionist versus intake or revenue platform
* Advice from founders who have scaled vertical SaaS or voice-heavy systems

Happy to give YC founders a live walkthrough.

launches.title: Ditto Bio – Evolutionary therapies for autoimmune disease
launches.tagline: We discover new drugs by harnessing parasite biology
launches.body:
We're [Adair Borges](https://www.linkedin.com/in/adair-borges-phd-729857222/), [Dennis Sun](https://www.linkedin.com/in/dennis-a-sun/), and [Emily Weiss](https://www.linkedin.com/in/emily-weiss-phd-939559124/), the founders of [Ditto Bio](https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/ditto-biosciences).

**We believe the world's best immunologists live inside of you.** 

TLDR; We transform parasite strategies for hacking the immune system into breakthrough drugs for autoimmune disease.

Viruses, ticks, and worms are the natural enemies of the human immune system. Over millions of years of experimentation, they've developed extraordinarily effective molecules to prevent your immune system from attacking them. This makes their proteins ideal drug candidates for autoimmune diseases, where a hyperactive immune system attacks the body's own tissues. We're mining the genomes of these organisms to translate these naturally occurring drugs into novel therapies.\
\
<https://youtu.be/4QFngdirw58>

**The Problem**

90% of drugs fail in clinical trials, when they are tested in humans for the first time. These failures come after companies invest 3-5 years and $15-20M “derisking” drugs in cells and mice. Everyone knows that cells and mice aren’t people, but without a smarter strategy, billions of dollars will continue to be wasted making drugs that will never reach patients.

**Our Approach**

We start with molecules that _already work_ in humans. Parasites have been running experiments on people for millions of years, creating powerful molecules to control the human immune system. Our AI platform identifies drug-like proteins from these organisms at scale, which we then engineer into safe, effective therapeutics.

**The Best Drugs Come from Nature**

Aspirin, penicillin, Botox, and GLP-1 agonists like Ozempic and Wegovy all originated as molecules from other organisms: aspirin from willow bark, penicillin from mold, and GLP-1 agonists from Gila monster venom. We're establishing parasites as the next transformative source of therapeutics.

**Our Team**

We’re three PhD scientists trained at top institutions (Harvard, Berkeley, UCSF, UCSD) with 40+ years of experience in computational biology, host-parasite interactions, and evolution. We worked together for 3 years as early scientists at another startup before founding Ditto.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=97563&key=user_uploads/2915094/304ef78d-d58a-499d-9ada-63096be7fb40)

**Our Data Moat**

Since founding seven months ago, we've analyzed 1M+ proteins across primate-infecting viruses, ticks, and parasitic worms. We've discovered thousands of proteins predicted to hit clinically validated human targets. Early experiments show that we have surfaced an untapped source of new drugs that act on high-value targets for immune diseases. Our proteins can achieve extremely tight binding (1–2 nM), among other drug-like properties.

We’re also building a tissue biobank that lets us map real-world immune memory to parasite proteins. This approach gives us a major advantage in tackling one of the biggest barriers facing all novel protein therapeutics: predicting and designing around immunogenicity.

The opportunity is vast: >98% of viral and parasite proteins remain uncharacterized. We're systematically mining this unexplored biology at scale to find and deploy nature’s best drugs.

**Our Ask**

If you’re an industry immunologist, biologics drug developer, or protein designer, please reach out at [founders@dittobio.com](mailto:founders@dittobio.com) to learn where our novel targets, natural scaffolds, and immunogenicity assays could make a difference for your drug programs.

launches.tagline: A home care agency that scales without administrative headcount
launches.body:
**TL;DR: [Cova](https://cova.care/) is a licensed home care agency in Michigan. AI agents run the entire back office, which lets us pay caregivers the highest base rate in the state, charge families less, and help unpaid family caregivers get paid through programs they didn't know they qualified for.**

<https://youtu.be/28Xmk3izvks>

**The problem**

This is one of the largest, fastest-growing markets in the country. 11,000 Americans turn 65 every day, and 70% want to age at home. 53 million people are already unpaid family caregivers, over $1 trillion in economic value every year that the system doesn’t capture.

But getting someone into home care is brutal. The application and paperwork alone take weeks of back-and-forth across a caregiver, a patient and their family, a doctor, and a state caseworker, with paper forms bouncing between all of them. Most of that time isn't care; it's coordination. Most families give up before care ever starts, and caregivers wait unpaid.

When care finally begins, caregivers suffer from missed payments and poor coordination, affecting patients downstream. All of this because existing agencies aren’t built to handle care at scale.

**What Cova does**

We own the full stack: Cova is its own home care agency serving Medicaid, LTCI, and private-pay patients, and AI agents run it end to end.

* **Weeks → days.** AI agents handle the applications and paperwork that normally drags on for weeks in just a few days.
* **Zero FTE overhead = highest caregiver pay in the state.** AI agents do the coordination work, so we carry no non-caregiver headcount and pass that straight to caregivers as the highest base rate in Michigan.
* **We get family caregivers paid.** Millions are already caring for a loved one for free and qualify for programs they've never heard of. AI agents find those programs and get them enrolled and paid.
* **We bill the payers directly.** Because we own the agency, we make money the way agencies do, billing Medicaid, MCOs, LTCI, and private pay, just with a fraction of the cost structure.

**About the team**

**Jordan Ibe (Co-Founder)** – Studied Computer Science & Statistics at Cornell University. Previously a Forward Deployed Software Engineer on Palantir’s Healthcare team and Software Engineer at Uber.

**Ansh Tandon (Co-Founder)** – Completed a BSE & MSE in Bioengineering at the University of Pennsylvania. Previously a Deployment Strategist on Palantir’s Healthcare team and Researcher at Daffodil Health.

**Our ask**

* Intros to Michigan MCOs (Medicaid managed care orgs) and long-term care insurance contacts
* Intros to Michigan hospital systems and providers: Henry Ford Health, Corewell, and similar
* Intros to Michigan discharge planners, hospital case managers, and social workers who place patients into home care
* Know a family caring for an aging loved one in Michigan? Send them our way! We'll check for free whether they qualify to get paid:[ cova.care](http://cova.care)

Ansh & Jordan, [founders@cova.care](mailto:founders@cova.care)

launches.body:
Hey everyone 👋

We're Pavan (PK), Gunin and Nirmit – co-founders of Ritivel.

## **TL;DR**

Ritivel is an AI-native workspace for regulatory and medical writing teams at life sciences companies. Our AI agents draft CTDs, CSRs, INDs, and BLAs in minutes instead of weeks, helping drugs reach patients faster.

**Ask:** Can you introduce us to regulatory affairs leaders or CISOs at pharma companies? Contact us at [pavan@ritivel.com](mailto:pavan@ritivel.com)

<https://youtu.be/VrqJtPDy_do>

## **❌ The Problem**

Every month a drug is delayed from reaching the market costs pharma companies \~$45M in lost revenue and more importantly, delays treatment for thousands of patients who need it.

Yet regulatory teams are stuck in a painful, months-long process to create FDA submissions like CTDs, CSRs, INDs, and BLAs:

**1. Information overload** 📚 These submissions require synthesizing thousands of pages of clinical data, prior submissions, and regulatory guidance which is an overwhelming task even for experienced teams.

**2. Document hunting & version chaos** 🔄 Teams waste hours digging through SharePoint folders, juggling multiple document versions, and chasing colleagues for the right files.

**3. Endless follow-ups** 📧 Regulatory leads spend their days sending reminder emails, tracking down missing inputs, and managing status updates across teams.

**4. Manual drafting bottlenecks** ⏳ Even with all the information gathered, the first draft alone takes weeks of painstaking work by highly specialized (and expensive) regulatory writers.

---

## **🔧 Our Solution**

Ritivel deploys AI agents that transform how regulatory teams work:

**Draft the most common document types like CTDs, CSRs, INDs, and BLAs in minutes** ✍️ Our agents generate comprehensive first drafts directly in Microsoft Word, following FDA formatting requirements and pulling from your existing clinical data and prior submissions. Every data point includes citations linked back to the original source, so reviewers can verify with one click.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=97327&key=user_uploads/939300/4d8b39f8-8230-4dcd-b654-c51b595d124e)

**Intelligent document retrieval** 🔗 Connected to SharePoint and Veeva, our agents automatically source the right documents from across your organization: no more digging through folders or chasing down files.

**Automated follow-ups** 📧 Integrated with Outlook, our agents handle reminder emails and follow-ups automatically, so you're not stuck chasing colleagues for missing documents.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=97327&key=user_uploads/939300/aa5a53c8-8d14-4c11-a20c-fecd59724cae)

**Accelerated project management** 🚀 By automating the document gathering and drafting loop, teams can focus on review and refinement rather than administrative overhead.

\
**👬 The Team**

We're engineers who previously built AI copilots at Microsoft Research. We saw firsthand that we could create better, more specialized copilots for complex workflows.

We started by selling a generic copilot to process-heavy industries like life sciences to understand their regulatory workflows. After 50+ conversations with pharma professionals, we discovered the critical bottleneck in regulatory submissions and built Ritivel to solve it.

**Hey everyone 👋!** We’re [Pari](https://www.linkedin.com/in/paridhilatawa/), [Frank](https://www.linkedin.com/in/frank-lee-/), and [Jin](https://www.linkedin.com/in/jinwong01/), co-founders of Illume. 

**TL;DR:** Illume is a 24/7 personal health companion that connects your wearables, nutrition, workouts, and lab results to give you personalized, actionable insights over text. 

**Join our private beta waitlist: [www.illumelabs.ai](http://www.illumelabs.ai). \
Watch Our [Launch Video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bsfFOzB0Nho):**

**Problem:** 

Health data is more abundant than ever, but it remains scattered. Nearly six in ten U.S. adults own a wearable or connected health device, and nearly one in three used an AI chatbot for health questions. People are generating more health data than ever and actively looking for help understanding it, but their data and guidance still live in separate places. 

We saw this firsthand as family members struggled to piece together glucose readings for diabetes and blood tests for cardiovascular risk, all while juggling a pile of fitness, nutrition, and health-tracking apps that never talked to each other. 

People increasingly turn to ChatGPT or Claude for answers, but without continuous context to their health, the advice is often generic, incomplete, and difficult to track over time.

**Our solution:** 

Illume creates one home for your health and gives you a personal health companion you can text. 

Today, you can: 

* Connect your wearable and automatically sync sleep, activity, and recovery data 
* Text Illume photos of your meals to log and understand your nutrition 
* Record workouts and track your training 
* Upload bloodwork and lab results 
* Ask questions about your health using the context of your own data 
* Receive proactive insights about what changed, what it might mean, and what to do next

For example, you can ask: 

* “Why am I so exhausted today? Make me a dashboard of all the relevant metrics!” 
* “How has eating late affected my sleep?”
* “Am I recovering well enough to train? Run a regression!”
* “What should I focus on before my next blood test?”

Illume connects patterns across your data that individual platforms can’t see, giving you a more complete picture of your health instead of another isolated score or dashboard. 

You can text your Illume agent for quick answers or use the platform to explore your data, trends, and history in greater depth.

**Our mission**

Our long-term vision is to make healthcare more proactive, continuous, and personalized. 

By combining continuous biometrics with nutrition, training, blood panels, and eventually genetic risk, Illume could help surface meaningful changes earlier and help people understand their susceptibility to conditions such as cardiovascular disease, diabetes, and Alzheimer’s. 

We want to help people move from asking, “What happened?” to understanding what may be changing and what they can do about it. 

**Who’s it for:** Illume is initially designed for people who are proactive about their health and longevity- especially lifters, biohackers, and anyone already using wearables, blood panels, CGMs, nutrition trackers, or genetic testing.  

**Who we are:** We’re three MIT graduates who met in freshman year! 

[Pari Latawa](https://www.linkedin.com/in/paridhilatawa/): MIT BS & MEng in CS + Molecular Biology. Previously conducted research at the Broad Institute, Eli Lilly, & MD Anderson. Founded EasyComm to build tools for children with Down Syndrome, and SparkED, a health-literacy nonprofit.

[Frank Lee](https://www.linkedin.com/in/frank-lee-/): MIT BS in Computer Science and Mathematics. Conducted RLAIF research for language models at MIT CSAIL and previously built agent systems at Windsurf.

[Jin Wong](https://www.linkedin.com/in/jinwong01/): MIT BS in Business Analytics. Previously conducted research at the MIT Media Lab and deployed coding agents at Windsurf. 

**Our ask:** 

**Join the private beta waitlist at [www.illumelabs.ai](http://www.illumelabs.ai).** We’ll invite an initial group of founding members to receive early access and help shape the product. 

**If you want to chat or can intro us** to someone in training, sports, longevity, and/or biohacking, email us at [founders@illumelabs.ai](mailto:founders@illumelabs.ai). We’d love to stop by, chat, and show you how Illume works!

launches.tagline: Juno helps people living with chronic illness reduce their symptoms and shorten the path to a diagnosis
launches.body:
Hey YC! 👋

We're [Isaac](https://www.linkedin.com/in/isaactolley/) and [Marshall](https://www.linkedin.com/in/marshall-gould/), co-founders of [Juno](https://junocompanion.com/).

**TL;DR:** Juno is an AI personal health assistant for the 1B+ people living with chronic illness. Over 80,000 people already use Juno to reduce their symptoms and shorten the path to a diagnosis.

**_Ask:_** Know someone living with chronic illness? Send them [Juno](https://junocompanion.com/) - we support a broad range of conditions including fibromyalgia, long COVID, POTS, ME/CFS, EDS, endometriosis, lupus, MS and many more.

<https://youtu.be/KIxKP8iUG10>

#### ❌ The Problem

Over 1 billion people live with chronic illness: fibromyalgia, long COVID, POTS, ME/CFS, EDS, endometriosis, lupus, MS and many more.

* Patients spend months waiting for appointments, then get 15 minutes to explain years worth of symptoms
* The average diagnosis takes 7.6 years
* Many now turn to ChatGPT and Claude for advice, but without continuous context, the advice is generic and rarely actionable

#### 👬 Our Story

We started building Juno after growing up with chronic conditions ourselves. Isaac waited 14 years for an eosinophilic bronchitis diagnosis. Marshall lives with ME/CFS and is still searching for something that helps. We spent the last year conducting research at Oxford and UCL to understand what makes people engage with medical chatbots, to allow Juno to ask the right questions at the right time and comprehensively understand each user’s health. 

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=101749&key=user_uploads/2576001/267e13c1-8296-4daf-8903-67cc817c56de)

#### 🩺 The Solution

Juno builds a longitudinal health profile from your conversations, biometrics, and medical history to provide:

* **💬 Personalised symptom advice** - guidance that actually makes sense for your body
* **📊 Continuous tracking** - symptoms logged automatically through natural conversation, by text or voice
* **🔍 Pattern detection** - identifies triggers and patterns over weeks and months
* **📄 Appointment-ready PDFs** - turn months of data into a summary your doctor can instantly understand

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=101749&key=user_uploads/2576001/18c9d3ee-5e7f-4b89-9465-09ecf9ea380e)

#### 📈 Where we’re at (after 6 months)

* **80,000 users** globally, grown primarily through our organic content
* **9,000+ five-star** App Store reviews

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=101749&key=user_uploads/2576001/277ec7df-3d59-4171-bb3b-e5fbda59ff1c)

#### 🙏 Our Asks

1. **Know someone with a chronic illness?** Please share Juno with them. We support a wide range of conditions including fibromyalgia, long COVID, POTS, ME/CFS, EDS, endometriosis, PCOS, lupus, MS, and many more. We'd love their feedback and hope it can be helpful.
2. **Intros to operators who've scaled consumer health products.** We're growing fast but Juno can reach far more people.

👉 Please share any feedback and contact us at [team@juno-chat.com](mailto:team@juno-chat.com)

 Download the app here: [https://junocompanion.com](https://junocompanion.com/)
