launches.tagline: You treat the patient, we handle the rest.
launches.body:
Hey everyone 👋 We're Adam and Nanda, the founders of **Taiga**.

**tl;dr:**

We automate the entire medical billing process for independent doctor's offices from coding to claim submission to denial management.

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HzQ13iVhbxk>

**❌ The Problem**

If you've ever talked to an independent doctor about billing, you know it's a nightmare.

* Independent practices either hire expensive billing staff, outsource to clunky billing companies, or doctors do it themselves after hours
* Claims get rejected for coding errors that could have been caught
* Denials pile up unfollowed, and revenue leaks everywhere

**🌲 How Taiga Works**

We automate the entire process.

* **Prior auths + benefits checks** — We check out the patient’s insurance before they come in to make billing seamless
* **EMR Integration** — We pull visit data automatically as soon as the visit completes
* **AI-Powered Coding & Scrubbing** — Our AI agents review clinician notes and generate procedure and diagnosis codes that are strongly supported
* **Claim Submission** — We submit clean claims directly to insurance
* **Denial Management** — We fight every single denial until the clinic gets paid. Every. Single. One.

**🧾 Proof**

> Taiga has been exceptionally easy to work with, with a responsive team always available to provide support. They successfully secured payment on a previously rejected claim by resolving an issue that had persisted for months; and they were able to accomplish that in just over a weeks time.

\- Neal Cheskis, LCSW

\
**👫 Why Us**

Both of our parents are doctors with their own practices. We watched billing cause them stress and lost revenue our entire lives. With our background in tech and our deep emotional ties to the space, we are able to provide faster payments and cheaper service so clinicians can focus on what’s important.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=100548&key=user_uploads/2909293/ba095169-9bac-4f96-97ab-753de18e4288)

**Talk to us!**

If you're a doctor or know a doctor, we'd love to talk. Visit [taigabilling.com](https://taigabilling.com)!

name: WonderTx
former_names: A Company in Stealth Mode Incorporated
long_description:
We’re an AI-native biotech, working on replacing needles with pills. Many drugs, like insulin or Ozempic, are wonderful except you have to inject them. We discover new molecules that you can take as a pill instead. Because the pills operate on biology which has been shown to be effective in people, rather than merely in animal models of disease, we avoid what has historically been the single biggest risk in drug discovery.  This should dramatically increase our probability of success.

There’s $200B of treatable diseases and validated human biology without a pill because discovery programs lack a tractable chemical starting point. This is a zero-shot inference problem, because these targets have no training data, so LLMs and other historical interpolative AI approaches are insufficient. Instead, we are building our own extrapolative frontier models that reason beyond their training data. Most critically, we have repeatedly validated our platform on both our own and partner programs. On 4 biologically- and structurally-diverse targets where we had zero training data, we successfully picked binders that were validated experimentally, with confirmation ranging from primary screen hits to crystallographic structures.
one_liner: Extrapolative AI to unlock First-in-Class drugs

question_answers.question: What is your long-term vision? If you truly succeed, what will be different about the world?
question_answers.answer: Imagine how drug discovery is done 80 years from now and it’s obvious that AI is going to be woven through every piece and every step.  No one believes that we will have less data, or that it will be easier to understand, or that we won’t need advanced statistical algorithms, or that the computers will be less capable.  There is an inevitability here.  But let’s not wait 80 years!  If we succeed then the path from conception to clinic for the toughest diseases, for the most difficult biological problems, becomes tractable.  Our practical outcome is simple: patients whose diseases cannot currently be drugged effectively or at all will live better longer lives.

Previously, cofounded Atomwise, the first company to deploy deep learning for structure-based drug design ($220+ million in funding; 100 hires; signed $5B in total partnership value with Sanofi, Bayer, Eli Lilly, etc; ran largest AI-driven drug discovery experiment w/ 600+ researchers in 30 countries).  Even more previous: PhD @ U of Toronto; inventor on 15 patents + applications; IBM Research; AI for Cornell’s world champion robotic soccer team.

launches.title: WonderTx: Extrapolative AI to Unlock First-in-Class Drugs
launches.tagline: Reindustrializing our life science ecosystem.
launches.body:
Our objective is to deliver first-in-class medicines against disease targets that cannot currently be drugged effectively or at all. Therefore, we are building a lights-out wonder drug factory, where AI runs the entire design-make-test loop. Linking superhuman judgment to robotic throughput is the path to reindustrializing our life science ecosystem, not through throwing human labor at the problem.

Our team has been working on this for over a decade, so we know that there has never been a better time to build this system.  Abe co-founded Atomwise, one of the first AI-for-drug-discovery companies.  We raised $220 million; hired 100 people; signed over $5B in total deal value with big pharma companies like Sanofi, Bayer, Eli Lilly, and others; and ran the biggest application of AI to hit discovery in history. Saulo solved the synthesizability problem in generative chemistry AI and wrote structural biology software that remains the standard toolkit (KVFinder; qFit3, STCRDab). Cam co-founded Xbox & Xbox Live (Microsoft) and has been a CEO, CTO, COO, and CPO across AI, biotech, healthcare, and consumer tech. 

Today, we see the convergence of critical enabling computational, physical, and economic trend lines. Agentic systems have become proficient orchestrators and tool integrators, as the frontier labs continue to extend the time horizons over which agents can operate; in our own hands, we have already compressed compound selection timelines 10x by replacing manual processes by agentic-run. The algorithmically-accessible chemical space has been growing exponentially for two decades, and the rise of cloud labs enables closing and scaling the design loop. Finally, the looming Big Pharma patent cliff means that the ecosystem is aligned on the value of innovative new assets. 

At WonderTx, we’re beginning by replacing needles with pills. Many drugs, like insulin or Ozempic, are great except you have to inject them. We discover new molecules that you can take as a pill instead. Because the pills operate on biology that has been shown to be effective in people, rather than merely in animal models of disease, we avoid what has historically been the single biggest risk in drug discovery.  This should dramatically increase our probability of success.

There’s $200B of treatable diseases and validated human biology without a pill because discovery programs lack a tractable chemical starting point, which makes this a zero-shot inference problem.  Because these targets have no training data, off-the-shelf LLMs and other historical interpolative AI approaches are insufficient. Instead, we are building our own extrapolative frontier models that reason beyond their training data. Most critically, we have repeatedly validated our platform on both our own and partner programs. On 4 biologically- and structurally-diverse targets where we had zero training data, we successfully picked binders that were validated experimentally, with confirmation ranging from primary screen hits to crystallographic structures.

launches.title: Voquill - Voice AI for Pathologists
launches.tagline: The AI coworker that helps pathologists work cases faster
launches.body:
Hey YC,

We’re Michael, Josiah, and Henry, co-founders of Voquill.

**TLDR:** Voquill is an AI coworker that helps pathologists write cases faster using their voice. Over the last 4 weeks. We’ve onboarded 25+ pathologists.

<https://youtu.be/Iw3n94o52Js>

**The Problem:** 

Pathologists are doctors who diagnose diseases by looking at tissues, cells, and fluids. They spend their whole day looking through a microscope, observing patterns, and then documenting their findings. These reports can be repetitive and tedious. **Pathologists bill a total of $30-$40BN each year** **yet a third of that spend goes to documentation**, not diagnosis, which is a massive drag on a field that's already short-staffed.

**Our Solution:**

Voquill is an AI coworker that helps pathologists write their reports faster. Think of it like an AI resident that listens to the pathologist as they work the case and drafts the report automatically. It learns the pathologists reporting style from their old cases, and ensures every report meets the bar for quality. We go beyond dictation and don't generate a transcript, but a finished sign-out ready report instead. This enables pathologists to spend more time on patient outcomes and sign out more cases.

There is already a shortage of pathologists when compared to the case demand. **This gap is expected to increase to 25% over the next decade.** We’re building Voquill to give pathologists the tools they need to work faster. 

**One More Thing:**

Voquill is being used by 25 pathologists from a leading F500 lab, saving each one \~20% in case writing time every day. We started with voice reporting because it's the highest-leverage moment in the workflow. We’ve since found that it's also the right moment to fix billing: as pathologists describe what they see, **Voquill suggests the optimal CPT codes, helping labs capture more of the $8B+ they currently leave on the table.**  

**The Team:**

Michael and Josiah previously worked at Techcyte, where they led the AI team and architected digital pathology systems. Henry was a Principal at Oliver Wyman, building AI and automation tools for F500 firms.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=101652&key=user_uploads/3291143/12ea3b4b-4f60-4a6a-8e43-07d68b0eb511)

**Our Ask:**

If you know any pathology labs or pathologists that sign out cases, please introduce us by emailing michael@voquill.com. Or, book a demo [here](https://calendly.com/michael-voquill/voquill-demo).

launches.body:
**TLDR**: Adialante builds compact and mobile whole-body MRIs. We already have $12.75M in LOIs, $30k in deposits, and our first system will be scanning by demo day.

---

##### **About Us:**

<https://youtu.be/iiRwpHPFIeM>\
\
"Disruptive Innovation describes a process by which a product or service takes root in simple applications at the bottom of the market — typically by being less expensive and more accessible — and then relentlessly moves upmarket, eventually displacing established competitors." — Christensen Institute

We’re [@Efrain Torres](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/1230366) and [@Parker Jenkins](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/1298954), the co-founders of [@Adialante](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/company/31434). We met on the first floor of our engineering dorm. And when we learned what disruptive innovation was, it captured us immediately. But what to disrupt? Trained as biomedical engineers, we both learned about MRI and were in awe of the clinical value. It can diagnose cancers, strokes, dementia, and more. Yet everyone said the same thing: MRI is not accessible.

So we knew what we had to do: disrupt the industry.

Over the past six years, we've invented new ways to do MRI, won millions in competitive grants, published research, secured patents (#12,625,209, #12,372,595, more to come), and built a team. And, now, we’re well on our way to disrupting the industry.

##### **Problem:**

We know how to 10x cancer outcomes: **you catch it early**. MRI is the most powerful cancer-detection tool in the world, yet systems cost millions to purchase, take months to install, and require high levels of technical skill. The result? We only use MRI when it's too late.

##### **Our solution:**

We've redesigned MRI from the ground up with new physics, algorithms, and hardware, all to bring cancer screening to all of us. Our MRIs:

* use 50% less hardware
* are 40% shorter and 80% lighter
* are whisper-quiet and much less claustrophobic
* and require no specialized infrastructure

All while maintaining the diagnostic quality patients need.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=101289&key=user_uploads/1230366/e7c9bf11-8868-457b-aced-78bd369559f5)

But like Waymo, we won't sell our hardware — we'll own and operate it. We'll bring our MRIs to clinics in mobile trailers, handle its operations, and continuously improve our AI software after every scan. We're an imaging clinic on wheels. So instead of a clinic waiting months and paying millions, clinics will wait hours and pay hundreds.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=101289&key=user_uploads/1230366/31ce218b-56df-4fc3-9450-5af5eea83895)

---

We're starting with prostate cancer. **Over 1M men every year require an MRI before a prostate biopsy, but virtually none of the urology clinics that treat them can offer one.**

After our per-scan fee, a clinic will collect the insurance reimbursement and make a profit. It's a win-win-win: we get the recurring revenue, they get a new revenue stream, and patients get the best imaging technology in the world. From there, the same piece of hardware expands to renal, breast, and brain scanning **until annual screening for high-risk cancers is the norm, not the exception.**

**Traction:**

* 6 clinics signed up
* $12.75M in LOIs for scanner utilization
* $30k deposited from a top ten urology clinic to reserve their spot in line
* MRI assembled

  ![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=101289&key=user_uploads/1230366/1fa5afed-cb5b-4f8d-a3f0-46a430043c0e)


##### **Asks:**

Intros to Urology clinics

Want to see our scanner? Shoot us a message! We’ll show you our system in person!

name: Lumius
long_description:
Ultrasound today is still mostly 2D. Clinicians have to imagine the 3D anatomy in their head while also moving the probe at the same time. This makes procedures like vascular access hard to learn and perform consistently, especially for beginners. ~50% fail on their first attempt. Hospitals also spend millions each year on 2D ultrasound training. Meanwhile, existing 3D ultrasound devices can cost >10× as much.

Lumius is building fast, smart, and accessible 3D ultrasound systems to eliminate this 2D guesswork. Our technology shows a clear, real-time 3D view of what’s inside the body. It works over a large volume, not just a thin slice. The device is also affordable, compact, and portable.

We are starting with vascular access, especially central line. Future use cases include blood clot detection, tumor diagnosis, and biopsy guidance. Our long-term vision is a universal 3D ultrasound platform that brings easy-to-use, real-time imaging to a wide range of clinical and eventually consumer applications.
one_liner: Fast, smart, accessible 3D ultrasound that anyone can use

launches.title: Lumius — The 3D Camera for the Body
launches.tagline: Fast, smart, accessible 3D ultrasound for everyone
launches.body:
**TL;DR:** Lumius is making real-time, accessible, and intelligent 3D ultrasound to advance beyond today’s widely used 2D ultrasound (500 million scans annually). Our vision is to make 3D ultrasound a universal camera for the body.

<https://youtu.be/bWlJD4_Bx4k>

**Backstory**

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=101060&key=user_uploads/3059826/d6bfe836-eb86-43cf-af8f-cf653183cebc)

Luca Menozzi, Chenhang Li, and I bonded over ultrasound during our PhDs at Duke. For years, it has bothered us that ultrasound looks largely the same as it did decades ago. It is safer and more accessible than imaging tools like PET, CT, or MRI, yet it has never quite become as widely used in everyday care as it should be.

**The Problem**

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=101060&key=user_uploads/3059826/a37bfe1d-0a2f-4738-ac51-c7628335098e)

The vast majority of ultrasound imaging today is still 2D. Clinicians have to maneuver a probe while mentally reconstructing 3D anatomy from flat images. That makes ultrasound hard to learn and difficult to use, especially for newer clinicians.  3D ultrasound does exist today, mainly for cardiac and fetal imaging, but current systems cost roughly 10x more than standard 2D ultrasound machines.

**The Solution**

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=101060&key=user_uploads/3059826/63de8f91-ad1d-4cd2-abdc-cbd2461fcd5f)

Our tech shows a clear on-the-fly 3D view of what's inside the body with AI assistance. Instead of relying on thin 2D slices, users see the full volume in context, eliminating the 2D guesswork that makes ultrasound difficult to use. 

Our device will be affordable, compact, and portable. AI integration will also make it context-aware and intelligent, guiding users by explaining what they’re seeing and what to do next. For example, automatically detecting and extracting blood vessels, nerves, muscle, and more. 

We're starting with vascular access, particularly central line placement. This is a procedure where \~50% of first attempts fail, especially among new clinicians. And hospitals spend millions each year training clinicians on 2D ultrasound. From there, we will expand to blood clot detection, nerve block imaging, tumor diagnosis, and biopsy guidance. launches.title: Infera – Control Lab Instruments with Natural Language
launches.tagline: Infera turns a plain-English experiment into a validated, instrument-ready run
launches.body:
### **⚡TL;DR**

**Infera is the Claude Code for scientific instruments.** Describe an experiment in plain English, and Infera turns it into a validated, instrument-ready run, handling the protocol logic, vendor scripts, data, and inventory across the instruments your lab already uses. One system, from intent to execution.

### 🤔 **The Problem**

Labs run on hardware from the future and software from the past.

The instruments are extraordinary. Mass specs identify thousands of proteins, flow cytometers read tens of thousands of cells a second, and cryo-EMs image at near-atomic resolution. These are the machines behind biomarker discovery, immunotherapy, structural biology, and drug development. But the software around them still looks like it shipped in 2003, and runs like it.

We've watched labs running \~6 instruments from 3+ vendors write a one-off script for every experiment, stitch outputs together by hand, and track inventory in a Google Sheet someone probably forgot to update last Tuesday. Scientists spend their week being human glue between machines that should already talk to each other.

### **🔍How Infera Works**

[**Demo Video**](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3GPze4X7AeA)

**I. Describe the experiment in plain English.** Infera asks the right questions, surfaces edge cases, and checks against your lab’s inventory and instrument state.

**II. Infera turns it into a run, accommodating both manual and automatable steps.** For programmable instruments, it generates vendor-specific scripts, executes, pulls the data back, and runs the analysis. For manual work like pipetting, gels, hand fermentation, etc., it's the context layer underneath: which step you're on, which reagent goes where, what could go wrong, and how others in the lab have run it before.

**III. The knowledge stays.** Every protocol, every validated run, every edge case becomes part of the system and checked against instrument constraints, lab SOPs, inventory, and prior experiments.

That last part is the hard part. It's what general-purpose LLMs can't do, and it's what enables a researcher to trust the output the way they'd trust a trained technician.

### 👩‍🔬 **Team**

Hi! We’re Chloe and Troy, and we're building Infera to close the gap between science and instrumentation.

* Chloe studied Mechanical Engineering at Harvard. She's been building research software and medical devices since before college (Regeneron STS Scholar), including a microfluidic device that detects harmful chemicals in household products, and has been doing research at places like Fred Hutch, Brigham and Women's, Harvard Medical School, and Pacific Northwest National Lab.
* Troy studied Computation & Neural Systems at Caltech, where he held an endowed research fellowship in a top research lab as an undergraduate. He's published two first-author cancer papers, holds a first-inventor agtech patent, and built and sold two companies before Infera.

Between us, we've run experiments by hand, written the scripts, and watched the whole system break when one person leaves. That's the problem we're building Infera to fix.

### **🎯Ask**

We're currently running pilots with Boston-area academic labs and cores. If any of these are you, reach out at [**hello@infera.bio**](mailto:hello@infera.bio):

* **Academic labs and cores:** know a PI or core director in proteomics, genomics, flow, automation, or screening? We'd love an intro, and we're happy to set up a pilot
* **YC founders with wet labs (diagnostics, therapeutics, synbio, tools):** we’d love to meet whoever runs your lab ops
* **Biotech and life sciences folks:** come say hi
* **Instrument manufacturers** whose customers wish the software were better, let's talk

launches.body:
Hey everyone 👋

We're Albert and Nathan from Harbor.

**TL;DR**

Harbor is a new system of record for data collection in clinical trials. Current systems are slow, clunky, and require hours and hours of manual labor. We're already live in five clinical studies and looking for more!

**Ask**: Can you introduce us to founders who might be running a clinical study soon or directors and VPs of Clinical Operations at CROs, medical device, and biotech companies? Contact us at [albert@runharbor.com](mailto:albert@runharbor.com)

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mBOYEL58RWw>

**🤦‍♂️ The Problem**

Everyone knows clinical trials are slow and expensive. Most people assume it's due to subject recruitment or regulatory requirements. But, a huge part of the problem is much simpler: manual data entry.

Clinical trial data is collected through a special database called an EDC (electronic data capture). Despite the massive amounts of spend, today's EDCs have not changed since the early 2000s. Companies spend 2-3 months manually configuring their EDC for each clinical trial. Clinical sites collect data from patients in the EHR or on paper and then spend hours entering that data by hand into the company's EDC. Finally, companies hire armies of people to literally fly to each clinical site and double check the data entered into the EDC. Despite the [FDA's guidance](https://www.fda.gov/regulatory-information/search-fda-guidance-documents/risk-based-approach-monitoring-clinical-investigations-questions-and-answers) **against** this way of doing things, it remains the de facto standard for the way clinical trials are run today.

At Harbor, we're changing that…

**💡 Our Solution**

At Harbor, we've built a new EDC platform that automates the most manual and tedious processes in data management, allowing sponsors and sites to spend more time with subjects, making sure the operations are running smoothly, and ultimately getting to database lock and regulatory submission faster.

* 👷 Our "Magic Build" feature takes clinical trial protocols and turns them into customized EDC builds within minutes. 
* ✍️ Our "Magic Capture" feature allows clinical sites to upload their source documents, whether electronic or paper, and Harbor enters the data into the EDC for them automatically.
* 🕵️‍♀️ As a result, sponsors get access to the study data in near real-time and their monitors don't have to fly all over the country just to compare what's on paper with what's in the EDC.

All of this is built into our fully validated and 21 CFR Part 11 and GCP-compliant software platform with roles, audit trails, and more, so that the data collected in Harbor can be used for regulatory submissions.

launches.title: BioStack Platforms: Realistic healthcare simulation environments
launches.tagline: We give AI labs the full post-training loop for healthcare
launches.body:
**Tl;Dr;**

We build realistic healthcare simulation environments where AI labs can train and improve their models before deploying them in the real world. Our environments use real-world clinical data to help models practice solving the hardest medical problems.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=101855&key=user_uploads/2459174/a27d387c-2ddd-4a28-98b6-c8a96da0503a)

**The problem**

Healthcare AI is learning from a cleaned-up version of medicine that barely exists. Real patients are messy. Their records are incomplete. Their labs are late. Their notes conflict. Their outcomes unfold over months, not in one prompt.

Doctors do not just answer questions. They make decisions with imperfect information, watch what happens, and adjust. That is the loop AI needs to perfect.

Today, AI labs have medical data. What they do not have are real clinical environments where models can practice, fail, get feedback, and improve.

**What BioStack does**

* **We turn real patient records into training environments.** Not clean textbook cases. Real longitudinal data: notes, labs, imaging, meds, vitals, diagnoses, follow-ups, and outcomes stitched into cases models will actually have to work through.
* **We build the tasks models train on.** Diagnose this. Order the next test. Adjust the medication. Flag the risk. Predict what happens next. The model makes a clinical move, then gets scored against outcomes, chain-of-thought reasoning, guidelines, and clinician review.
* **We give AI labs the full post-training loop for healthcare.** Data, evals, reward functions, benchmarks, and simulation environments, so models can practice real clinical work instead of just memorising medical exams.

[https://drive.google.com/file/d/1NvcLS2usN_bl4GE_tW7QVN5Ia-MGl8M6/view](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1NvcLS2usN_bl4GE_tW7QVN5Ia-MGl8M6/view?usp=sharing)

**Backstory**

We started the company in Oct 2025 and burned through two pivots before we found the thing that pulled us in.

First, we tried building multi-agent systems for biology research. It sounded right on paper. In practice, biology workflows are messy, fragile, and full of assumptions that have to be tuned by hand. One wrong parameter compounds downstream and suddenly nobody trusts the output. Scientists also were not ready to hand over real work to agents that still felt too brittle. We killed it after two months.

Then we tried going deeper: generate preclinical drug discovery data ourselves, at scale, through our own lab facility. Again, it sounded ambitious. Again, it broke on contact with reality. It was capex-heavy, slow, operationally painful, and not truly venture-scalable. Worse, our edge was basically cheaper offshore execution. That is not a moat. That is a race to the bottom. We killed that too.

The third idea found us.

The best companies are born in the customer’s office. For us, it happened on a sales call.

We were pitching drug discovery data to one of the largest human data companies in the world. Halfway through, the conversation shifted. They did not want another generic data vendor. They asked if we could deliver high-quality clinical data for a six-figure contract.

**That call changed the company.**

We realised the real bottleneck was not just raw data. AI labs need the full post-training stack for healthcare: clinical data, simulation environments, evals, reward functions, and verifiable tasks that make models better at real medical work.

So we followed the pull.

Today, BioStack is building simulation environments for healthcare AI. We have expanded from one customer conversation into 17 customers and prospects, including top AI labs, and we are seeing demand across data, evals, and RL environments.

We did not arrive here through a brainstorm but got dragged here by the market.

**Asks**

* **Do you know** **anyone** **working on a AI models or agents** advancing current capabilities through multimodal applications, nuanced reasoning, or domain-specific expertise?
* **Do you know of companies that require raw medical data?** We supply longitudinal high quality scans, EHR, and notes and we’re happy to send over samples.
* **Have referrals for RL engineers / researchers?** We’re always looking to hire RL engineers who specialise in fine-tuning methods such as SFT, PEFT, and RL.
* **Spread the word** - send us ideas for data types that you think are valuable and spread the word!

**Feel free to reach out** at: [sanat@getbiostack.com](mailto:sanat@getbiostack.com) / [parth@getbiostack.com](mailto:parth@getbiostack.com)

launches.body:
**TL;DR:** Biomanufacturing is bottlenecked by experiments that take years and don't transfer across products. We're building foundation models for biological manufacturing, validated against wet lab data, so decisions that take 6-18 months today can be made in hours, saving $100M+ per program.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=101683&key=user_uploads/3323269/c03e8ad1-e7f1-4b0c-8417-b22137f847af)

**The problem**

Biologics development is one of the slowest, lowest-yield engineering disciplines in the modern economy. A single CHO cell line campaign costs $5-10M and 12-18 months. Multispecific antibody programs routinely fail at CMC. Every month of delay on a blockbuster costs pharma $100M+ in lost revenue.

Every product team rebuilds the same process knowledge from scratch because:

* nothing transfers across products, scales, or sites
* the data that exists sits trapped in PDFs, batch records, and proprietary silos
* existing tools optimize one product at a time and need expert tuning
* AI-for-bio has focused on drug discovery and overlooked the value in manufacturing

Pharma spends over $100B annually on biologics development and manufacturing, and ships processes with yields and timelines that haven't fundamentally shifted in a decade.

**What we built**

**The first foundation models for biomanufacturing**, designed to close the data gap incumbents can't.

Our first model, Echo, predicts manufacturing outcomes more accurately than standard hybrid models, and any pharma or CDMO can adapt it to their workflow instantly. We're extending the same architecture to cell line engineering, multispecific developability and CMC risk, and upstream aggregation (HMW%) prediction.

The complex biologics wave is the immediate wedge: 600+ molecules in active clinical trials, \~15 approved, and a CMC-heavy profile that punishes one-product-at-a-time tooling. Foundation models that transfer across products are the only way to keep up.

**Our story**

I'm Daniel Mukasa, founder and CEO. I’ve spent much of my career at Caltech, Merck, MIT, and the Broad doing drug discovery, just to watch our carefully optimized drugs get killed by manufacturing problems. I’m building the tools we need to fix that across the full biomanufacturing stack.

**Our ask**

**Pharma, biotech, and CDMO intros**. Specifically, cell line development, process development, and CMC leads working on biologics, multispecific, cell and gene therapies, and AAV delivery systems. Also open to BD conversations with platform companies sitting on proprietary process data.

launches.title: Plena Health: The AI operating system for specialty medical practices
launches.tagline: The full stack AI operating system for specialty medical practices
launches.body:
**TL;DR**

Plena is the full stack AI operating system for specialty medical practices. We automate the administrative work that keeps clinics running — referrals, fax intake, scheduling, procedure compliance, records, and collections. Everything that isn't the medicine.

**In 8 months, we've grown 17x and crossed seven figures in contracted ARR.**

So far we cover six specialties across eight states, all on annual or multi-year contracts, with 80% of our growth through word-of-mouth.

<https://youtu.be/xWw9kNYckHQ>

**The Problem**

My mom is a doctor. Plena's office sits inside her clinic — she was our first user. I grew up watching her run a practice, and the pattern was the same in every clinic I later embedded in: a doctor's day eaten by everything that isn't medicine.

Independent specialty practices are squeezed. Staffing costs rising, reimbursements tightening, payers using automation to deny and downcode claims.

Meanwhile, practices run critical workflows across EHRs, clearinghouses, portals, fax, spreadsheets, phones, and email. A single referral: read the fax, match the patient, extract clinical details, check insurance, update the EHR, attach documents, route tasks, chase missing info. That's one workflow. Practices run dozens daily.

Most software adds another portal, another login, another vendor. Point solutions cover a slice. Staff stitch the rest together.

\
**Why Point Solutions Can't Get You to Labor Replacement**

The real goal isn't automating one workflow. It's labor replacement — and you can't get there one feature at a time.

No single piece of software works for all specialty practices. Cardiology, GI, urology, ortho are too different from each other. Even two clinics in the same specialty are too different. Off-the-shelf can't cover the surface area.

So we took a Palantir-like approach: a base platform of reusable building blocks — workflow primitives, EMR integrations, agent harnesses — that lets us assemble exactly what each practice needs. Deep discovery, build to spec, stand it up in a day or two. Every engagement feeds the platform, so the next build is faster. That's the flywheel.

AI is what makes this newly possible — final-mile customization at speed is exactly what AI is good at. And it's why we're an easy yes: no rip-and-replace, no retraining. We slot into what practices already run and take more off their plate over time.

**How Plena Works**\
Plena automates workflows end-to-end across the systems a practice already uses — EHRs, fax, phones, clearinghouses, payer portals, patient communication. We don't replace those systems. We don't ask staff to learn a new one.

Some competitors force practices to migrate into a walled garden — abandon the EMR, retrain the team, rebuild data flows. That's why their sales cycles are slow. We do the opposite: we live inside what's already there, and quietly take over the rote work end-to-end.

Customers start with one painful workflow — referrals, collections, scheduling — then expand as they see it work.

\
**Where This Goes**

We start as an automation layer on top of what practices already have. Over time we cannibalize the rote work and the other vendors a practice is stitched together from — until the EHR is just a database we read and write to. From there, even the EHR becomes a turnkey switch instead of the migration nightmare it is today.

That's the system specialty practices end up running on.

\
**Our Story**

Eyad and Ahmed were both raised in medicine — Eyad's mom and Ahmed's dad are doctors. The combination — engineers who grew up watching practices run — is why we kept seeing the operational problem when other founders saw something else.

Eyad is a Waterloo engineering grad — Datadog and Shopify before Plena, 3 years embedded in clinics. Ahmed built tier-zero infrastructure at AWS, with a background in nuclear systems before that. Specialty practices didn't need another lightweight tool — they needed infrastructure.

\
**Our Ask**

Intros to independent specialty practices, administrators, and physician owners — especially orthopedics, GI, dermatology, ophthalmology, ENT, urology, and multi-location groups. Best fit: high admin volume and disconnected systems.

launches.body:
TL;DR: We’ve built the foundations of a pharma in the age of superintelligence: data partnerships, biology models and autonomous research agents. We have SOTA results on finding overlooked drugs and predicting clinical trial success rates. 

Hey everyone! We ([Sanjukta Bhattacharya](https://www.linkedin.com/in/sanjukta-b-82b541198/), [Christian Gensbigler](https://www.linkedin.com/in/christian-g-a2594029a/), and I) started Atlas Discovery to get treatments to patients who need them most.

**The problem:** Today's pharma works for only \~150 diseases. Below roughly $150M in expected revenue a program never gets funded, because the cost of developing a drug is fixed by the knowledge work it requires, not the size of the market. 10,000+ diseases remain without an approved treatment even where the biology is tractable. Meanwhile, there are 100,000+ existing drugs, and barely 1% of the drug-disease combinations have ever been tried. The bottleneck is no longer supply of compounds; it's the judgment needed to search that space and run the trials, and the removal of human coordination costs.

**Our** **thesis** is that AI will drop the cost of drug development enough to push the viable threshold from \~$150M toward \~$15M, opening a \~$500B market incumbents have structurally ignored. A company built for that world needs three things: proprietary data, models that predict clinical trial outcomes, and agent systems that replace knowledge work. We use agents to repurpose existing drugs for the long tail of diseases, then run the clinical trials faster and cheaper. 

**Progress**: In three months we've built the first version of all three layers. Data: an 8 figure LOI with an AI lab and 6 figures in contracted revenue. Models: state-of-the-art clinical trial prediction results published at three conferences,. Agents: three rare disease foundations are now testing drugs surfaced by our agents. 

On drug repurposing using agents, we see nearly 5x improvement over current frontier LLMs. Read more about this benchmark [here](https://atlasdiscovery.bio/repurposingbench.html).

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=107031&key=user_uploads/774885/cf98d216-1d2c-45a0-99c9-ef87d2b7b296)


We've also shown that models trained on in vitro cell data (Latin for "in glass") and mouse data can translate to gains in predicting patient response to drugs in human clinical trials.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=107031&key=user_uploads/774885/6813bfeb-e5c9-47ec-9b9e-89362cf8eb15)

We’ve also shown SOTA results in being able to predict clinical trial success when trained on over 100,000 clinical trials data and evaluated on a held out set of 10,000 trials. Read more [here](https://atlasdiscovery.bio/clinical-trial-prediction-with-ai-agents.html)

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=107031&key=user_uploads/774885/23aff312-7161-4be9-b4af-3273d469bd5d)

We’ve presented our research in 3 top conferences (ICLR, CSHL, ICML) and shown that new AI architectures like discrete diffusion can learn these gene expression patterns and predict response to treatments with over 10x improvement in accuracy while training on 50x less data.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=107031&key=user_uploads/774885/fa2a6593-751d-448b-a67b-e232e3e07ffb)

Reach us at [founders@atlasdiscovery.bio](mailto:founders@atlasdiscovery.bio)

launches.body:
Hey YC!

I'm Christine Park, founder of Lattice Health. We make sure the AI that hospitals deploy on medical imaging keeps working after it goes live.

Launch video: <https://youtu.be/p0l029tsmhs>

Website: <https://www.latticehealthai.com/>

**The problem.** Hospitals are adopting medical imaging AI faster than ever. But once a model is live, almost no one can answer a basic question: is it still working? Models drift, a scanner upgrade or a shift in the patient population can quietly degrade accuracy, and performance often varies across patient groups. Most of that goes unseen today, and it's the hospital, not the vendor, that carries the risk.

**What we built.** Lattice is a monitoring and governance layer for deployed imaging AI. We plug in beside the imaging pipeline as a read-only observer and continuously check each model: how well it agrees with the radiologist's read, whether it's drifting over time, and how it performs across patient subgroups. Then we turn that into the evidence hospitals need for safety, governance, and compliance. Lattice never touches patient care, it only watches, so if Lattice stops, care continues.

**Why now.** AI is moving into clinical use under a wave of new expectations from the FDA, ONC, and the ACR, and they all point to the same gap: continuous post-deployment monitoring. Hospitals are on the hook for it and have almost no tooling to do it.

**Our ask.** We'd love intros to health system and radiology leaders, CMIOs, and anyone running AI governance at a hospital, as well as imaging AI vendors who want their models monitored well in the field. And if you have thoughts or hard questions, drop them in the comments or email me at [christine@latticehealthai.com](mailto:christine@latticehealthai.com)

### **About us**

We’re Haris and Yaman. We have deep experience within enterprise AI for healthcare.

Previously, we both worked at Anterior (backed by Sequoia, NEA, Microsoft AI’s CEO) — where we built, sold and deployed our clinical AI platform to US health plans to remove major operational bottlenecks.

### **Problem**

Developing drugs and medical devices is complex and expensive (for drugs: 10-15 years, $1-2B).

The cost of drug development is growing exponentially (doubling every 9 years). This is known as Eroom’s Law (inverse Moore’s Law).

**The most critical** process in development is getting regulatory alignment, and ultimately, approval from the FDA.

Biotechs and medtechs outsource this work to regulatory consultants.

This work is highly manual: searching through legacy FDA databases, researching and reading hundreds of publications, reading FDA guidance documents, data analysis, authoring thousands of pages per filing, etc.

Consultants take months to years, and charge 6–7 figures per engagement, to deliver FDA regulatory strategy, authoring and submission services.

These consultants also price hourly. Therefore, using AI to go faster would cannibalize their revenue. So they have no incentive to deliver work faster.

### **What changed**

**AI can automate 90% of this work**. Consultants can now focus on the 10% where their expertise and judgement is actually needed.

We hire the best FDA consultants in the industry (ex-FDA, decades of experience, hundreds of FDA filings).

We pair them with our AI platform to deliver higher quality FDA regulatory services **significantly** **faster and at lower cost.**

We also offer **fixed, milestone-based** pricing. Clients only pay once we deliver each agreed milestone.

We handle the end-to-end workflow, from establishing payer contracts to enrolling each provider. We collect and validate organization and provider data according to each state and payer’s requirements, and submit on the organization's behalf. We then monitor status and compliance on an ongoing basis.

The platform gets smarter with every submission, contract, and claim. Our browser agents learn to navigate payer portals more effectively. # TL;DR: We’ve created the last probiotic you’ll ever need - personalised, constantly improving, while also generating valuable data.

### 

# What we do and why

Your gut is the most unique part of your body, different enough that the same probiotic can work for one person and do nothing for another. Most probiotics disappoint because they’re one formula for everyone, and in any gut most of their strains never establish. GutGutGoose makes a probiotic that won’t work for any gut but yours: we sequence your microbiome, find which strains can establish in the microbes you already have, compound those into your formula, and re-sequence you weeks later to confirm they took hold.

It’s for people who’ve tried things for IBS, bloating, digestion, mood, weight or GLP-1 symptoms without luck. If it doesn’t work you get your money back, and retesting shows how your gut changed, so you know it’s not a placebo.\
\
<https://youtu.be/Cn6oGduZosc>

The innovation is accurately predicting which bacteria will live in a gut, which is extremely hard. It’s built on two peer-reviewed models, MICOM and AGORA2, and more than 7,000 metabolic reconstructions of gut bacteria, and it finds the strains that can hold in your gut’s community. On two published human cohorts, its predictions matched what actually established 84.7% and 76.7% of the time, and we reproduced the first at 78.1% ourselves. Off-the-shelf products manage under 5%. Once we can control which bacteria live where, we can run precision interventions in the gut and engineer it.

We’re a supplement today and can’t treat disease, but each cycle produces a record of one gut, one intervention, and the result. That record makes each customer’s next formula better, and across thousands of people it becomes the first longitudinal dataset of the human gut responding to known, controlled changes. Our vision is to use changes in metabolic pathways over time to predict Alzheimer’s, dementia and Parkinson’s a decade before symptoms appear.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=108277&key=user_uploads/991771/50caffe3-e0c9-44e5-9212-da1bbabc0e00)

# Traction

We gave a talk at an endometriosis event, and 20 of the 50 people joined our waitlist. The first night we opened paid deposits, we called five people from that list at 7:30pm. Three picked up, and we managed to get seven sign ups, they were so excited they referred and paid for their families that night. Five of the 20 referred someone else, and our traction has only grown since.

# Team

The GutGutGoose founders winning the YC product pitch

Leon started university at 14 and spent four years at a $3bn YC unicorn. After we started GutGutGoose, he built a pharmacy, now doing $4M a year, to fund the science behind our engine. Anis joined in September; he co-built the model, runs operations, and is the youngest ever to win Queensland’s Math Olympiad. He’s on a Chancellor’s Excellence Scholarship in AI and Data Science, and (fun fact) was once the world’s number one Catan player.

launches.body:
Hey everyone — we're **Chang and Bryan**, the founders of **Insurf**.

American health insurance is f\*\*\*ed: chosen by guesswork, enforced by denial. We built the engine that fixes both halves.

**TL;DR**

**Surely** computes the lowest-cost plan for anyone. **Inveto** fights denials for real clinics across Texas, Georgia, and California, and each contract-authorized, de-identified outcome becomes coverage data nobody else has. Everything Inveto learns, Surely knows.\
\
[https://drive.google.com/file/d/1x5B44OPfZxd-32UBeGT-0a5WVdMf3Jnl](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1x5B44OPfZxd-32UBeGT-0a5WVdMf3Jnl/view?usp=sharing)

**The problem: America picks health plans from one number**

More than 20 million Marketplace enrollees choose coverage off the sticker premium. That guess is expensive.

• In our data, the lowest-premium plan was the lowest-cost option in **0 of 2,000 simulated years**.

• In one example, the cheaper sticker would have cost **$8,052 more** in a single bad year.

• That's one person. Multiply the risk across a family. Across a company.

• This year alone, **four million Americans** found out what their plans actually cost — and walked away from coverage.

We compute.

**Surely — the cost engine**

Surely ranks all plans by what they'll actually cost: premiums, deductibles, drug tiers, networks, out-of-pocket caps. Every number sourced from government filings.

**Inveto — the denial workbench**

Clinics upload a denial and the clinical record; Inveto produces source-cited, physician-signed appeals and supported prior authorizations. Live with real clinics across Texas, Georgia, and California today.

**The moat is the join**

Every contract-authorized Inveto outcome becomes rights-cleared data about what plans actually do, including approvals, denials, appeals; Surely reads all of it. **What plans cost + what plans do. Nobody else has both.**

**Why now**

In 2028, health plans stop renewing automatically: 20 million+ people will re-choose coverage every single year — the largest forced re-shop in the history of American health insurance. $150 billion a year in premiums, re-decided annually.

And employers are next. The federal government projects **800,000 companies and 11 million+ people** will switch to ICHRA, where employees choose their own plans. That's a **trillion-dollar shift**. With Insurf, employers can expect to save **\~$5,000 per employee, per year**.

**Who we are**

Two friends who met during orientation at Brown. Chang got into medical school at 17, then worked a pharmacy counter watching thousands of people pay out of pocket for what they were promised. Bryan placed internationally in CS and physics competitions and has published IEEE research since high school.

**Our ask**

• Tired of overpaying for health insurance?

• Weighing ICHRA, or trying to cut your company's benefits spend?

• Running a specialty clinic buried in denials and prior auths?

See how much your company can save here: [insurf.io/audit](https://www.insurf.io/audit) or email [founders@insurf.io](mailto:founders@insurf.io) — we'll show you exactly what you'd save.

**Everyone sells plans. Nobody prices them. We compute.**

The tool then dies locally on the builder’s computer, because IT (correctly) won't let anyone deploy a tool touching PHI without first-class authentication and permissioning. Our first customer had multiple employees who had each built useful tools and dashboards locally, but couldn’t actually share these with coworkers or connect to their core practice data. Within weeks of implementing Floracene, they were able to consolidate their BI tooling into Floracene and shipped 4 net-new to production.

A staggering ~$200B is spent on administrative software in healthcare every year in the US. Tens of thousands of those companies still run core operations on spreadsheets, and we're at the top of the first inning of AI adoption.

Asaph and Jonah met on the hospitals team at Palantir two years ago, and have each spent the last four years in the plumbing of US healthcare: claims, eligibility, and payor contracting. Asaph was an early PM at Garner. Jonah was a founding engineer at Metriport (YC S22) after starting his own fax-automation startup for fertility clinics.

name: Rasyn
long_description:
We builds foundational AI models for chemistry. Almost nothing you buy is a single chemical. Products like datacenter coolant, GPU thermal paste, paint, and glue are formulations, which are mixtures of around ten ingredients each, and demand for them has grown quickly because of AI and EVs.

Designing a new formulation is essentially a search problem, because there are more possible mixtures than anyone could ever test, and none of them can be predicted in advance. As a result, bringing a single formulation to market today takes three to five years of trial and error in a lab.

Our models predict how a mixture will behave far faster than the standard methods used today, which lets us design new formulations in weeks rather than years, at a fraction of the cost. To prove this, we used them to invent three chemicals that never existed before, including a PFAS-free coolant for datacenters, and we have since synthesized and patented all three.

We are already working with some of the largest manufacturers to design formulations for them, and we are building our own lab to generate the data that will train our next models.
one_liner: Making chemicals 100,000x faster

launches.title: Rasyn: One place to run any Chemistry task
launches.tagline: Towards a General Intelligence for Chemistry
launches.body:
**Hey!**

We're **Rasyn**, and we built a platform called **Marigold**. Give it any chemistry task in plain language and it pulls the literature, reads your files, picks the tools, sets up and runs the calculations on its own machine, and hands back the numbers along with its reasoning what it did to get them. 

It's live at [app.rasyn.ai](http://app.rasyn.ai); here's a short demo: <https://youtu.be/ru1BeRBlRec>

\
**Here's the team:** \
Our team has worked at NASA JPL, and researched with scientists from Nvidia and Deepmind. Our team has worked on softwares serving 50 million users, and their research was used by frontier AI labs including OpenAI and Meta. Our team studies Computational Chemistry at Caltech, has done Total Synthesis for 4+ years, and researched alongside Nobel Laureates, so they have faced these problems firsthand. They'd lose hours deciding which tool to call next, moving outputs between disconnected tools, and running a single program at a time.

**Problem:** \
Chemistry has countless software. There's one for predicting a structure, another for proposing a route, another for reading a spectrum. None of them talk to each other, so you're stuck feeding outputs between them; this clerical work is where the time goes, none of which is science.

\*\*Solution:\*\*\
We tried coding agents first. They're built to write software, so a chemistry task gets handled as a scripting problem and the chemistry goes unverified. Marigold checks between steps and stops when something doesn't hold.

It runs on its own machine, so it installs and executes what it needs. It works with the tools chemists already use, submits jobs to your cluster, and runs on whatever model endpoint you have, so your data can stay in the building. In the demo we hand it four thousand compounds and ask which are worth screening. It does the whole thing itself.

Longer term we're building toward a general intelligence for chemistry. Marigold today reasons over existing tools, and that's where we start.

**The Ask:**

This is only the first version; it will break. And we'd like it to break in front of chemists, so if you run any sort of chemistry, please try it and tell us where it falls over. 

We'd also love intros to any lab doing chemistry, computational or wet, since we want to sit down and work through a real problem with people. 

Happy to answer any questions!

launches.body:
**TL;DR: Stratum builds AI agents that automate the slow, manual processes governments run on. We're starting with application review - clearing backlogs in a fraction of the time and saving agencies tens of billions a year.**

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=108362&key=user_uploads/1648613/f70bb601-955f-4c6c-946f-8d8c90d04fa6)

**The problem**

Governments run on manual work. Millions of complex processes - reviews, approvals, filings, claims -are still handled by hand, one file at a time, on software built long before AI existed.

Take application review. Every permit, license, patent, drug approval, and benefits claim in America is reviewed by hand, one file at a time. Millions sit in queues while people wait months and years: veterans on disability ratings, families on pensions, builders on permits.

The tools reviewers open every morning were built long before AI. So the work stays manual, and the queue only grows.

This isn't one broken workflow. It's how the entire government runs.

**What Stratum does**

Stratum builds AI agents that automate the slow, complex, manual processes governments run on.

We're starting with application review.

A reviewer uploads an application and selects the rubric to check it against. From there, an agent takes over: it plans the review, works through the file end to end, and checks every requirement, routing each step to the right model.

A human approves every outcome, and every step is fully auditable.

The difference is scale. Instead of one reviewer on one file, hundreds of agents run in parallel — clearing an entire backlog in the time it once took to review a single application.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=108362&key=user_uploads/1648613/e23f9409-271f-4879-95aa-374eb37ae64f)

**Who we are**

We're Vihaan (VJ) and Raj - brothers.

Vihaan (CTO): founding engineer #3 at Cadastral (acquired by Legora), waterloo dropout.

Raj (CEO): led GTM at Deel, dropped out of CS grad school at the University of Bath.

Application review is the first workflow. The mission is to integrate AI across every vertical inside the government.

Governments are among the largest, most complex organizations on earth — and almost none of it has been touched by modern AI. We're changing that, saving agencies tens, eventually hundreds, of billions a year and making the government one of the most efficient institutions in the world.

Looking to bring AI into your agency? Reach out to the team or book a demo [stratumindustries.co](https://stratumindustries.co/)

**TL;DR**

Stratum builds AI agents that clear the U.S. government's backlog. A reviewer drops in an application, picks the rubric to check it against, and an agent plans, executes, and reviews the file end to end. Hundreds run in parallel with a human approving every decision, so a backlog that used to take months clears in the time it took to review one file.

Every permit, license, patent, drug approval, grants and benefits claim in America has to be reviewed by a government adjudicator, on software built decades before AI. The result is millions of applications stuck in queues, and real people waiting months or years: veterans on disability ratings, families on pensions, builders on permits. The approval isn't the problem. The software it runs on is.

2. An agent reads every page and checks the file against that rubric.
3. Every step routes to the model that reviews it most accurately for the least cost.
4. Anything missing goes back to the applicant as one specific request.
5. The officer gets the whole file summarized, with every citation behind it, and approves or denies it.

Hundreds of these run in parallel in the cloud, with full auditability at every step, and a person always makes the final call.

launches.title: TareBio: Vaccines for any cancer or infection in weeks
launches.tagline: We make personalized or population-level vaccines reverse-engineered from the immune system. We have already cured cancer in mice and are vaccinating our first patient within the year.
launches.body:
**TL;DR:** Our platform develops **personalized** or **population-level** vaccines for **_any_ disease** in weeks by **changing _only one input_**: the immune imprint. Instead of trying to predict which antigens might work, we read out immune cells already fighting the disease in the body and reverse-engineer antigens that activate them. We've already run our platform end-to-end and created a vaccine that cured cancer in mice. We will be vaccinating our first patient within the year.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=108804&key=user_uploads/431020/46cdbd4d-72d9-4231-a781-01a886dd82a4)

View our launch video here: <https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ty7jA8ecY2o>

**The vaccine bottleneck**

For 200+ years, vaccines have been designed using the same workflow: study a pathogen or tumor, _predict_ which antigens might trigger protection, vaccinate, and hopefully generate a good immune response. This works for simpler infections. It has struggled for decades on complex diseases like HIV, TB, Hep C, and nearly _every cancer_. Currently, vaccine design is treated as a prediction problem.

**What we do differently**

Instead, we treat it as a readout problem. The **immune system has _already solved_** antigen selection in the body, it knows what it's responding to and the best immune cells for the job. So, we flip the whole process around:

1. Capture the immune cells already responding to a cancer or infection, the "**immune imprint**"
2. Use this imprint to directly identify, or “**reverse engineer**”, activating antigens
3. Build a **vaccine** from those antigens

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=108804&key=user_uploads/431020/31744f0e-4a44-4aa9-aa2e-29d174a8d30a)

The same platform works for **_any_ disease** by changing one input: the immune imprint. Function over prediction, no constrained search space, and the output is a vaccine that can generate durable immunity in the body, not a transient antibody conjugate or cellular therapy.

**Proof**

We built the full platform in mice and ran it end-to-end: identified antigens from the immune imprint of the cancer, designed a vaccine from them, and **cured lymphoma in mice.** Nothing about the technology is specific to lymphoma, it generalizes to any cancer or infection. We are using our technology to create both personalized (n=1) and population-level vaccines.

**Why us**

I'm Eta Atolia, founder and CEO. I built this platform over the last 8 years as part of my MD-PhD at UCLA-Caltech with funding from The Gates Foundation. Before this, I did my undergrad at MIT with most of my time dedicated to cancer immunotherapy and infectious disease research at the Koch and HMS. Our scientific advisory board includes Darrell Irvine, PhD (Vice Chair of Immunology at Scripps, Former MIT Professor of 22 years, world-renowned vaccine engineer) and Manish Butte, MD, PhD (Chief of Immunology at UCLA and expert rare disease clinician).

**Our ask**

We are actively working with organizations and individuals to create both population-level vaccines and personalized treatments.

Helpful things as we build:

* If you have **patient tumor** **or** **blood samples**, please reach out.
* Intros to **biotech + pharma** and **vaccine teams** for partnerships.
* **Immunologists, oncologists, infectious disease specialists,** and **ML engineers** who want to build this with us.

If any of this resonates, reach out at [contact@tarebio.com](mailto:contact@tarebio.com).

launches.tagline: A research lab, for one.
launches.body:
Hey YC! We're Alfredo and Ranad, the founders of Omanta.

**TL;DR: Omanta creates a personalized research lab around a single patient. We integrate a patient’s complete medical record, personal genomics, and use AI to take on the most complex cancer cases. Our researchers tackled GitLab co-founder Sid Sijbrandij’s case, helping bring him into complete remission.**

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EkZaq_fENqI>

\
**Why this matters**\
If you're a cancer patient, you'd think the hardest cases have entire teams dedicated to solving them. The reality: most doctors have about 20 minutes per patient, while the science never stops moving. New discoveries emerge every day, yet reaching standard clinical care can take over a decade (\~17 years on average). Physicians make high-stakes decisions with limited time, and even the most difficult cases rarely have anyone whose full-time job is to interrogate every layer of that one patient's disease and push the newest science toward their treatment.

That's the gap we built Omanta to close.\
\
**What we do**\
We meet patients wherever they are in their journey. We integrate their complete medical record and personal genomics with AI and clinical evidence to understand the molecular drivers of their disease. Then we map every existing therapy against their biology, and if the right therapy doesn't exist, we build it, from cancer vaccines and immunotherapies to highly targeted radioligand therapies.\
\
We've worked on some of the most complex cancer cases in the world. Most notably, **Alfredo was the genomics lead for the personalized therapeutic campaign behind GitLab founder Sid Sijbrandij's complete remission**, partnering with leading institutions to pursue personalized mRNA/DNA vaccines, CAR-T programs, drug repurposing, expanded-access therapies, and continuous molecular monitoring. We've seen what becomes possible when the full force of modern science is organized around a single person, and Omanta brings that depth of investigation to every case.\
\
**Why us**\
We met eight years ago working on early CRISPR cancer research and have been building toward this ever since.

* **Alfredo Gonzalez, PhD (CEO)** — translational genomics. Led the year-long investigation of 25TB of sequencing and molecular data for Sid Sijbrandij, key missing information in existing genomic reports, and uncovered actionable findings that reshaped his therapeutic strategy, including personalized mRNA/DNA vaccines, CAR-T, expanded access, drug repurposing, and continuous monitoring. PhD at UCLA, where he built one of the world's largest centralized multi-omic datasets for rare tumors. Previously at the Broad Institute (Cancer Dependency Map, validating targets from large-scale CRISPR screens) and Harvard's Wagers Lab.
* **Ranad Humeidi, PhD (CSO)** — chemical biologist. Earned her PhD in Chemical Biology from Harvard in three years, where she identified a druggable mechanism in ulcerative colitis that became the basis of a multimillion-dollar GSK collaboration. Built and directed a multimillion-dollar scientific program centered on a single rare-cancer patient, then went on to direct scientific strategy for 12+ medically complex patients after standard options were exhausted. At the Broad, she co-created and co-led a fellowship turning scientific discoveries into companies.

\
**Our ask**

* Intros. If you or someone you love is facing a difficult cancer diagnosis, we want to hear from you.
* We're also looking to connect with physicians who want a dedicated research team behind their most complex cases.
* Reach us here on Bookface or at [alfredo@omanta.com](mailto:alfredo@omanta.com) & [ranad@omanta.com](mailto:ranad@omanta.com).

**Peptides are like Claude Code for your body. Your biology is the prompt.**

**TL;DR:** RonanRx personalizes GLP-1s like Ozempic and other peptides to _your_ biology, because you are not average. Connect your lab results, wearable data, and medical history once. Our HIPPA compliant Al turns them into a plan which a licensed doctor prescribes, adjusts every cycle, and ships to your door. Start with a text at [**RonanRx.com**](http://RonanRx.com).

### **Big Pharma Makes 1 Drug for Millions.**

Peptides are the most personalizable medicine we have, and everyone has different biology. GLP-1s like Ozempic help you lose weight. Others help you recover faster, sleep better, live longer. Telemedicine often prescribes them like a vending machine: fill out a quiz, a doctor you’ll never meet rubber-stamps it, and you get the same molecule at the same dose as everyone else. Nobody reads your data and adjusts when your body responds differently than the “average patient.” That’s not medicine, it’s a spreadsheet.

Connect your health data once, and we run the complete feedback loop for personalized medicine:

* **Your biology in one place.** We sync your labs, wearables, medical history, and treatment response into a single health profile.
* **AI turns data into a plan.** It reads how _you_ are responding and proposes the next move: dose, formulation, what to add.

* **Delivered to your door,** and every outcome improves your next protocol.

Instead of treating the average patient, we personalize your treatment continuously as your body changes.

Building a healthcare company isn’t for tourists. We’re native to the space, and passionate about fixing what’s wrong. launches.body:
# Lumeria is the Oura Ring for Skin:

TLDR: Lumeria is the Oura Ring for Skin: the Lumoscope clips onto your phone, scans your skin with the same multispectral light used in clinics, and Lumi, your AI skin coach, reads that history to personalize recommendations for you, so your routine is built on your data instead of someone else's.

Preorders are open at the $199 founding price until **August 16. After that, the price only goes up**. <https://lumeria.skin> 

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=W-tz9FIQiOg>

## ❌ The problem

Anthea’s sister spent eight years chasing her eczema.

The cause turned out to be dust in the carpet.

No one caught it because no one was recording anything. Her skin was reacting to her sleep, her home, her products, the air around her, and none of it existed as data. Every dermatologist that took months to see started from zero. Every product she tried was a guess.

That is the **$190B** skincare industry in one story. It runs on guessing.

Lumeria ends that: it captures the missing data layer that gives you the power to understand and own your skin's health data, from home.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=109979&key=user_uploads/3470868/08058377-6a96-414b-b03e-44ff36f8622a)

## 🔬 How it works

The Lumoscope shrinks the multi-spectrum imaging dermatology clinics use into a clip for your phone. Press it against your skin and see yourself in three kinds of light: true color (RGB), UV, and cross-polarized.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=109979&key=user_uploads/3470868/76776eef-52f9-4416-827c-36c74760f8dd)

For the first time, you see what your mirror can't: a breakout building days before it surfaces, sun damage hiding under flawless-looking skin, where inflammation is building up.

Each scan becomes an objective read (hydration, redness, evenness, pigmentation, texture, pores) plus a score out of 100 and a skin age, so you can understand your progress.

Track them over time, and Lumi tells you exactly what to do. 

* It finds the cause, linking your breakouts to habits you'd never think of, from your sleep to your cycle to the pillowcase you forgot to wash. 
* It recommends products from a database of 18000+ products + ingredients, matched to what your scans actually show works.
* It hands your dermatologist 90 days of images, trends, and context in one tap.
* And it compounds: every scan adds to a history and increased understanding of your skin’s relevant context.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=109979&key=user_uploads/3470868/c36570ca-4042-47bc-beb4-5f1a27014d6a)

 It works across every skin tone. It is private and encrypted by default. 

## 👥 Why we built this

Anthea, our CTO, lived with this problem: suffering from eczema that would not heal, five months to reach a dermatologist, four misdiagnoses. She is an engineer who worked on computational biology at Google and Boehringer Ingelheim. Maryanne, our CEO, is a skincare creator with 25M+ views across her UGC portfolio, exited her first biotech company by 19, and still could not explain her own breakouts until Lumeria. We understand the helplessness people feel with their skin, so we built what was needed.

We are patent pending, shipping in Fall 2026, and built on 150+ interviews and 2 clinical partnerships with dermatologists and patients.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=109979&key=user_uploads/3470868/d7da4795-da8c-4edd-8c96-58e540656067)

name: Gamgee
long_description:
​Gamgee began with Rosie, founder Paul Conyngham’s dog. After surgery, chemotherapy and immunotherapy failed, Rosie was given months to live. Paul used AI and genomic analysis to identify targets in her tumour, then worked with scientists at UNSW to produce what is believed to be the first fully computationally designed mRNA cancer vaccine delivered to a dog. Following treatment, several tumours shrank significantly and her quality of life improved

Gamgee is building an end to end platform for personalised mRNA cancer vaccines for dogs. We sequence a dog’s tumour and healthy DNA, identify mutations unique to its cancer, and design a vaccine that teaches the immune system what to attack. We manage the entire process- from vet intake and tissue collection through genomic analysis, vaccine production, treatment and response monitoring

​We are now turning that one off effort into a repeatable clinical system. Gamgee is running clinical trials in Australia, working with vets, oncologists and specialised laboratories, and accepting cases globally. Our goal is to make personalised cancer treatment accessible to every dog that needs it- and use each case to improve the treatment for the next
one_liner: Curing cancer. Starting with dogs.

launches.title: Gamgee: Personalised mRNA cancer vaccines for dogs
launches.tagline: Input the tumour. Output the vaccine. 300+ dogs on the waitlist.
launches.body:
**We believe that AI meets biology is the biggest opportunity of the 21st century.** We are using AI to build autonomous systems that read biological failure, discover how to control it, and design precise repairs. We are starting with the first computationally personalised mRNA cancer vaccine for dogs.\
\
**My dog Rosie was dying of cancer.** I designed her an mRNA vaccine. Several of her tumours shrank 50-75%. I am not a biologist - I spent 17 years in machine learning. Doing it by hand took a year and around $20,000. Gamgee is turning that process into software. Our target is a vaccine design in 48 hours and an end-to-end cost of $2,000

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-Jb41jTc0U0>

**How it works**

* We **send you a collection kit** to take to your vet or veterinary oncologist. Your vet collects the tumour and matched healthy samples, which are returned for DNA and RNA sequencing.
* Our software finds and ranks the mutations worth targeting, and keeps the evidence behind every call.
* **Out comes an mRNA vaccine** design ready for manufacture. Gamgee designs the vaccine and oversees and coordinates every step through to administration by the treating veterinarian.

\
**The market**

Approximately **six million dogs** are **diagnosed with cancer** every year in the United States, and cancer is the leading cause of death in adult dogs. Owners who pursue specialist treatment spend thousands on surgery, chemotherapy and radiation.\
\
\
**The compounding data advantage**

Every dog we treat returns sequencing, immune and outcome data for a species where datasets remain scarce. That data improves target selection, which improves the next vaccine, which produces better data. We are not just early to the problem - we are the ones accumulating the data that solves it.

\
**Proof so far**

* Full computational pipeline built and executed end-to-end as a non-biologist using AI
* 50-75% shrinkage in the responsive tumours. 
* Microscopic analysis found substantial IBA1+ macrophage and CD3+ T-cell infiltration in Rosie’s responsive lesions, with little in the non-responsive tumour.
* Second-generation vaccine completed and ready
* Over a billion impressions on Rosie's story.
* Backed by Y Combinator (S26) 

Rosie was one patient. Our next step, already well underway, is a clinician-led trial in 30 dogs to evaluate safety, immune response and clinical outcomes.

\
**Why dogs first, and not only dogs**

Most modern dog breeds were created within the last few hundred years from small founder populations and then bred within closed gene pools. This concentrates inherited cancer risk, leaving many breeds unusually prone to particular cancers.\
\
Pet dogs develop cancer naturally, not in a laboratory. Their immune systems are intact and their disease progresses on timelines that let us learn quickly. Dogs are a real market in their own right and the fastest place to get good at personalised cancer vaccines.

\
**Our ask**

* **If your dog has cancer, please do get in touch about our upcoming clinical trial.**
* Veterinary oncologists and specialty hospitals who want to be a trial site.
* Investors in longevity or personalised medicine - would rather meet you before the trial reads out than after.

We are building Gamgee so that no other dog waits for hope which arrives too late.

Reach me at [paul@gamgee.io](mailto:paul@gamgee.io) or [gamgee.io](http://gamgee.io)\
\
I love you Rosie.

launches.title: Hubble: Retrieve medical records other APIs can't
launches.tagline: Your user verifies their identity once, and we return their medical records through one API.
launches.body:
**TL;DR:** Hubble gives your product a patient's medical records through a single API. Your user verifies their identity once, and we assemble their records from across the providers they've seen and return them for your AI agent to use. Where APIs are not sufficient, we keep going with AI (browser and voice agents). Every request runs on the patient's individual right of access.

**The problem**\
If you're building something that needs a patient's records, there's no clean way to get them. A patient's history is scattered across every provider they've ever seen, and each system is its own island. Most APIs returns the patient-portal subset rather than the full record, and coverage is inconsistent because every health system sets up its integration differently. So most teams either build per-provider integrations for months, fall back to faxes and manual portal logins, or push the problem back onto the patient by asking them to track down their own records or remember a login they set up years ago and have long since lost.

**What Hubble does**\
Your user verifies their identity once, and we go get their records so you don't have to.

* **One verification, no work on your end.** The patient verifies their identity in a couple clicks. After that, assembling the records is our job, not yours and not theirs.
* **We don't stop at the portal subset.** We connect into EHRs and HIEs where they work, and when an API comes back empty we keep going.
* **Browser and voice agents for everything else.** Agents submit the patient's request through provider portals and call records departments on the patient's behalf, working the phone trees so nobody on your team has to.
* **Built on the patient's right of access.** Every request runs on the patient's individual right of access. They review every source we request from and can revoke at any time. Every retrieval is logged.

**About the team**\
We're the team behind the AI agents at Grow Therapy and Amazon's One Medical, used by millions of patients. Prabha was Grow's first PM building and scaling their AI agents. Aaron built the AI infrastructure at One Medical serving 1M+ clients. (Fun fact: we've known each other for over a decade.)

* Intros to anyone building AI products on patient data, in digital health, care delivery, life sciences, or legal tech.
